## Summary

The phase's mechanical foundation is in far better shape than the 2026-08-02 audit implies, and the count of net-new work is materially smaller than the audit's arithmetic. Three findings reset the plan's size:

**First, SC1 is already 90% satisfied and the repo already owns the right mechanism.** `app/layout.tsx` uses `next/font/google` with `Inter({ subsets: ["latin","latin-ext"] })`, which downloads font files at build and self-hosts them. I verified empirically against the existing build output: `.next/static/chunks/*.css` contains **zero** `https://` references, and every `url()` resolves to a local `../media/*.woff2`. The Google-Fonts-CDN problem the audit calls W-2 lives in the *design project's* `tokens/fonts.css`, not in the repo. What 01.1 actually owes SC1 is (a) swapping Inter for the Cena pairing and (b) an automated tripwire. Critically, `subsets: ["latin","latin-ext"]` provably covers every RO and HU diacritic for all three families — verified codepoint-by-codepoint against Google's own metadata API, not assumed. All three families are OFL 1.1, so self-hosting is permitted; but **IBM Plex Mono carries the Reserved Font Name "Plex"**, which is a concrete legal argument against hand-rolling a `pyftsubset` pipeline and in favour of shipping Google's own official subsets through `next/font`.

**Second, the "10 missing primitives" figure is wrong in both directions.** Six of them (`Select`, `Radio`, `Switch`, `Field`, `Tabs`, `Tooltip`) are one `shadcn add` away, exist under this repo's exact `radix-nova` style, are built on the `radix-ui` package already installed, declare no `cssVars` (so they will not mutate `app/globals.css` mid-migration), and pull exactly one transitive addition (`separator`, via `field`). Two of them are not missing at all: `IconButton` is `Button size="icon"` — the existing `button.tsx` already ships four icon sizes — and `Toast` is already covered by `sonner`, which has no `radix-nova` registry entry to replace it with (HTTP 404, verified). That leaves at most two genuinely hand-authored items (`Icon`, `Tag`), both trivial and neither carrying Radix behaviour. Set against that, the audit's "16 primitives" is **not a superset of what must be re-skinned**: the repo also ships `alert`, `avatar` and `dropdown-menu`, which the DS's 16 never names and which will look mixed-system if left alone. SC2's "all 16" understates the surface by three.

**Third, the SC2 regression invariant is far safer than expected, with exactly one land mine.** The 47-file / 462-test suite is green in 50.06s (run this session), and grepping it for appearance coupling returns essentially nothing — the only hits are in `tests/lib/theme-width-scale.test.ts`, which reads `app/globals.css` and Tailwind's own `theme.css` as oracles rather than asserting on rendered classes. That file is the one hard constraint on the token layer: **if the Cena token set introduces a `--spacing-<name>` that collides with a Tailwind container name, the test fails until a matching `--max-width-*`/`--min-width-*` shield is added.** The land mine is elsewhere: `tests/venues/venue-form-languages.test.tsx` asserts `checkboxFor("ro").disabled === true`, and `disabled` is precisely the mechanism that causes G-01-13. Fixing G-01-13 by re-enabling the control would change that test's meaning and violate SC2 — so the fix must keep `disabled` on the visible Radix control and carry the value in a sibling hidden input instead.

One conflict the planner must resolve rather than discover: SC1's literal wording ("no third-party font **or asset** request on any page") is already false and will stay false — `app/(auth)/components/GoogleOneTap.tsx:422` loads `https://accounts.google.com/gsi/client`, which is ACCT-01's Google sign-in, a feature, not an oversight.

**Fourth, and now verified: the qr-menu template is a good visual spec and a poor coverage claim.** Of its 11 self-declared requirement IDs, **one holds, ten are partial, none is outright false.** The pattern in the failures is consistent and predictable: every claim confined to *diner-side display* holds well or fully, and every claim that reaches into an owner-side surface (MENU-08/09, ACCT-02), into persistence (LANG-06), or into architecture (LANG-05, DINE-04) does not — because a static design template structurally cannot carry those. Two findings have consequences beyond the template. The allergen vocabulary is **7 of the EU's 14**, while the template README asserts "Allergens are the EU set" — a false claim on the one surface PROJECT.md flags as legally load-bearing, and it omits **peanuts** as a category distinct from tree nuts. And LANG-05's mechanism — reading `navigator.languages` on first paint — is incompatible with the prerendered, CDN-served diner page CLAUDE.md mandates; language detection has to move to `Accept-Language` at the edge with one static page per (venue, language), which also solves LANG-06's persistence gap for free.

**Primary recommendation:** Ship the token layer as `@theme inline` blocks imported into `app/globals.css` — but **do not copy `tokens/fonts.css`**, which is a Google-CDN `@import` and would regress SC1 on its own. Keep the Cena pairing on `next/font/google` with `subsets: ["latin","latin-ext"]` and no custom subsetting pipeline. Add the six registry primitives before re-skinning any surface. Gate SC1 with an allowlist-based source tripwire whose single entry is the Google Identity Services script. Adopt the qr-menu template as a **visual and behavioural spec to re-implement** — never as code to port — and carry its 11 verdicts forward verbatim so phases 2–7 inherit the residue rather than the claim.

## Requirement Coverage Verdicts — `templates/qr-menu/`

**This is the answer to CONTEXT.md D-05 and the highest-value output of this research.**

Method: for each of the 11 requirement IDs the template's README claims, read the requirement text in `REQUIREMENTS.md`, then read what `QrMenu.dc.html` actually does — markup, the `DCLogic` data model, the `T` string tables, and `lang()` / `money()` / `wantsPhoto()` / `renderVals()`. The README's table was treated as the claim under test, never as evidence.

### Scoreboard

| Req | README's claim | **Verdict** | One-line reason |
|-----|---------------|-------------|-----------------|
| DINE-02 | "Table identity comes from the scan" | **partial** | Displays the table label; nothing about venue resolution or published-state gating |
| DINE-04 | "`offline` shows the saved-menu banner" | **partial** | Banner design holds; copy fails D-07 and describes the wrong failure model |
| DINE-05 | "Tapping a dish opens the sheet…" | **HOLDS** | Complete and faithful — the only unqualified pass |
| DINE-06 | "Vegetarian / vegan / gluten-free filter chips… Allergens are the EU set" | **partial** | Dietary filtering is excellent; **the allergen set is 7, not 14** |
| MENU-08 | "Lunch · Dinner · Drinks" | **partial** | Diner-side switcher only; MENU-08 is an owner-CRUD requirement |
| MENU-09 | "each with its service hours; the menu on now carries the gold badge" | **partial** | Display half only, and `now` is a hardcoded literal — zero time logic |
| MENU-10 | "Sold-out dishes stay listed, badged…" | **partial** | Diner-side display is fully right; owner toggle + propagation absent |
| LANG-05 | "read from `navigator.languages` on first paint" | **partial** | Detection *policy* holds; the *mechanism* is architecturally incompatible |
| LANG-06 | "pills override the detection for the rest of the visit" | **partial** | Control holds; "for the rest of the visit" is in-memory only |
| THEME-03 | "the `photos` tweak switches the whole template" | **partial** | Switch holds; zero-photo is a subtraction, not a design; "some" is unsolved |
| ACCT-02 | "the `currency` tweak formats every price" | **partial** | Formatting convention transfers; FX is demo scaffolding; owner surface absent |

**1 holds · 10 partial · 0 does-not-hold.**

> **How to read "partial".** None of these is a defect in the design work. A diner-surface template cannot cover an owner-side requirement, and the README's error is one of *scope claiming*, not craft. The value below is in knowing precisely **which half transfers** so phases 2–7 adopt that half and budget for the residue.

---

### DINE-02 — *Scanning a table QR opens the correct venue's published menu in a mobile browser with nothing to install* → **partial**

**What holds.** The table-identity display: `dict.table(this.props.tableLabel || '7')` renders "7. asztal / Table 7 / Masa 7" as a mono, uppercase, letter-spaced eyebrow above the venue name (line 32). Localised in all three languages via `T[lang].table(n)`. The mobile-first shell — one column, `max-width:520px`, `min-height:100dvh`, centred, `--shadow-sm` — is the right container and is directly adoptable.

**What does not.** Everything DINE-02's risk actually lives in: slug→venue resolution, the published-vs-draft gate (nothing in the template distinguishes them), 404 behaviour for an unknown or unpublished venue, and table-code encoding. `tableLabel` is a free-text prop with a `'7'` default — there is no notion of a table *identifier* that a QR could encode, nor of validating one.

**Residue for Phase 2.** Routing, published-state gating, unknown-venue/unknown-table states, and the QR payload format. Adopt only the eyebrow pattern and the shell geometry.

---

### DINE-04 — *If the network fails during load, the diner still sees the last-good version of the menu rather than nothing* → **partial**

**What holds.** The banner *design*: full-width, above the cover, non-dismissible, `--warning-soft` background with `--warning-border` bottom rule and `--warning-text` copy, a 16px `Icon name="info"` and a single sentence at `--text-sm`/1.45 (lines 18–23). That is a correct, calm treatment and should be adopted as the pattern.

**What does not.**

1. **The copy fails D-07.** Template EN: *"You are seeing the saved menu. Prices refresh as soon as you are back online."* D-07 requires timestamped and specific: *"Saved menu from 14:20. Prices and sold-out items may have changed."* The template's string carries neither a time nor the sold-out warning, and D-07's rationale is precisely PROJECT.md's named risk that "a diner orders something that has been off for a month."
2. **There is no real timestamp to carry.** `updatedLine` is `dict.updated + ' 4 · 8 · 19:04'` — a hardcoded literal (line 459). The footer *looks* like it shows freshness and does not.
3. **The copy describes the wrong failure model.** "as soon as you are back online" asserts a *client*-offline model with automatic recovery. CLAUDE.md's architecture is ISR stale-serve: the page the diner is reading was prerendered and served from the edge; what failed is *background regeneration*, not the diner's connection. The diner may be perfectly online. A string that tells them to reconnect is misleading, and it also implies an auto-refresh the page does not perform.
4. **No mechanism.** `offline` is a boolean prop the design tool toggles. Legitimately out of a template's scope — the mechanism is ISR's documented last-good serve — but it means DINE-04's actual guarantee is unevidenced here.

**Residue for Phase 2.** A real `generatedAt` on the prerendered page; a D-07-compliant string in all three languages, authored through the D-04 register and landed as a Copywriting Contract row; and a decision on *how the page knows it is stale* (the honest signal is prerender age, not `navigator.onLine`).

---

### DINE-05 — *A diner can browse categories, view an item's detail (description, photo, allergens, dietary tags, calories/macros, variants)* → **HOLDS**

The one unqualified pass, and it covers the hardest surface.

| Clause | Evidence |
|---|---|
| browse categories | Sticky category rail (lines 61–71) with `jumpTo()` → cubic-eased smooth scroll to `#cena-cat-<id>`, offset 108px for the sticky header. Sections carry matching `<h2 id>` (line 94) |
| description | line 151, `--text-base`/1.5 |
| photo | lines 142–146, gated on `sel.photo` |
| allergens | lines 202–203 — `allergLine` joins localised names with `' · '`, with an explicit `t.none` fallback ("No allergens marked."), **plus** the disclaimer at line 209 |
| dietary tags | lines 205–207, uppercase chips on `--accent-soft` |
| calories/macros | lines 187–199 — a 4-up grid: kcal, protein, carbs, fat, each value in mono over an uppercase label |
| variants | lines 160–180 — selectable rows, `1.5px` border, selected state on `--surface-selected`, and **the sheet's headline price updates from the selected variant** (`sel.price = money(variants[vi].p)`) |

Two things worth calling out as genuinely good: the `t.none` allergen fallback is an explicit empty state rather than a blank line, and the always-present disclaimer ("Allergen details come from the kitchen. Tell your server if you have an allergy.") is exactly the posture PROJECT.md's EU-FIC constraint requires — the obligation sits with the restaurant. **Keep that line, in all three languages.**

**Two caveats that do not change the verdict but bind the implementation.**

- **The sheet has no accessibility.** It is a `div` with backdrop-click-to-close and `e.stopPropagation()`. No `role="dialog"`, no `aria-modal`, no focus trap, no Escape handler, no focus restore, no accessible name. This is audit D-2's problem surfacing inside a template. **Re-implement on Radix `Dialog`** (already in `components/ui/dialog.tsx`) and take only the visuals: bottom-anchored, `max-width:520px`, `max-height:88dvh`, `--radius-sheet` on the top corners, `--shadow-xl`, `backdrop-filter:blur(3px)` over `--surface-overlay`, and the two keyframes (`cenaSheet` 16px rise, `cenaFade`). Honour `prefers-reduced-motion`, which the template does not.
- **The category rail is derived from non-empty sections** (line 445: `cats: sections.map(...)`, and `sections` is `.filter(s => s.items.length > 0)`). So applying a dietary filter changes which categories exist. Defensible, but it means the rail can reflow under the diner's finger — decide deliberately rather than inheriting it.

---

### DINE-06 — *A diner can filter or identify items by dietary tag / allergen* → **partial** ⚠ *legal weight*

**What holds, and holds well.** Dietary filtering is the best-designed interaction in the template: three chips (Vegetarian / Vegan / Gluten-free), **AND** semantics (`picked.every(d => item.diet.includes(d))`), 44px minimum touch targets on both states, a checkmark icon on the active chip, a running count line ("3 of 9 dishes" / "3 fogás a 9 közül" / "3 din 9 feluri"), a "Clear filters" action that appears only when filters are active, and a genuinely helpful empty state ("Drop one filter, or ask your server — the kitchen can adapt more dishes than the menu shows"). Allergen *identification* also holds: allergens print as plain chips on every row (lines 109–111) and in the sheet — so a diner can identify without filtering, which is what the requirement's disjunction allows.

**What does not — and this is the finding with legal weight.**

**The allergen vocabulary is 7, not 14.** `AL` (lines 238–246) defines exactly: `gluten, milk, eggs, fish, nuts, celery, sulphites`. Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011 Annex II mandates **14**.

| # | Annex II substance | In template? |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Cereals containing gluten | ✅ `gluten` |
| 2 | **Crustaceans** | ❌ |
| 3 | Eggs | ✅ `eggs` |
| 4 | Fish | ✅ `fish` |
| 5 | **Peanuts** | ❌ — **collapsed into `nuts`; Annex II lists peanuts separately from tree nuts** |
| 6 | **Soybeans** | ❌ |
| 7 | Milk (incl. lactose) | ✅ `milk` |
| 8 | Nuts (tree nuts) | ✅ `nuts` |
| 9 | Celery | ✅ `celery` |
| 10 | **Mustard** | ❌ |
| 11 | **Sesame seeds** | ❌ |
| 12 | Sulphur dioxide / sulphites | ✅ `sulphites` |
| 13 | **Lupin** | ❌ |
| 14 | **Molluscs** | ❌ |

`[CITED: Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011 Annex II — corroborated across multiple independent summaries; see Sources]`

**Why this matters more than a missing enum value.** PROJECT.md's constraint is that "EU food information rules require allergen information to be available to consumers, and the obligation to get it right sits with the restaurant." Cena's obligation is therefore not to *declare* allergens — it is to **not make compliance structurally impossible**. A 7-value vocabulary means a restaurant serving prawns, satay, hummus or mussels physically cannot declare them. That is a product defect with legal consequence, and the peanut omission is the sharpest edge of it: peanut is among the most severe allergens and is a *separate* Annex II category precisely because tree-nut avoidance does not imply peanut avoidance.

**The README's claim "Allergens are the EU set" is false.** Do not carry it forward. This is exactly the failure mode D-05 exists to catch.

**Also absent:** any *filter* by allergen. Only dietary tags filter. DINE-06's "filter **or** identify" is satisfied by identification, so this does not sink the verdict — but if a later phase wants exclude-by-allergen (arguably the more useful interaction for an allergic diner), it is net-new.

**Residue.** The full 14-value vocabulary in hu/en/ro, with peanuts distinct from tree nuts, before any diner surface ships. The chip *display* pattern transfers as-is. Note the chip styling — `--text-2xs` on `--surface-sunken` in `--text-subtle` — is the lowest-contrast, smallest-type combination on the whole surface; it must be in the SC4 pair list.

---

### MENU-08 — *An owner can create multiple menus per venue (e.g. lunch, dinner, drinks)* → **partial**

**Category error in the claim.** MENU-08 is an **owner** requirement — it is about *creating* menus. A diner template cannot cover it.

**What holds.** The diner-side consequence: a horizontal rail of menus (lines 44–59), each showing label + service hours + a 2px accent underline when active, switching via `setState({ menu, cat: null })` — and note it correctly resets the category anchor on switch. Localised labels and localised `hours` where the value is not a literal time range ("All day" / "Egész nap" / "Toată ziua"). This is a good, adoptable pattern and Phase 2 needs it.

**What does not.** Owner menu CRUD — creation, naming, ordering, deletion, assignment of items to menus. None of it, and none of it can be here.

---

### MENU-09 — *An owner can schedule a menu to show automatically by time of day* → **partial** *(weakest of the three MENU claims)*

**What holds.** The diner-side *display* of a schedule: `hours` per menu ('11:30–15:00', '17:00–23:00', 'All day') and a gold "Now" badge (`Badge tone="warning"`) on the live one — the single napfeny element on the screen.

**What does not — all of it, structurally.**
- **`now: true` is a hardcoded literal** on the `dinner` menu (line 224). There is no clock read anywhere in the file, no timezone handling, and no derivation. Copying this ships a badge that says "Now" at 4am.
- The initially-selected menu is `state.menu = 'dinner'`, also hardcoded — the template does not even select the "now" menu.
- `hours` is a display string, not a schedule. There is no start/end model, no timezone, no day-of-week, no overlap resolution.
- The entire owner-side scheduling surface MENU-09 actually names is absent.

**Residue for Phase 3.** The schedule data model (start/end/days/timezone — and note `venues.timezone` already exists and is nullable for EUR, which is why `lib/validation/venue.ts` warns "a silently wrong timezone breaks time-of-day menu scheduling (Phase 3) in a way nobody notices until service"), the owner scheduling UI, the server-side "which menu is live now" derivation, and the interaction with ISR (a time-based transition cannot be driven by `revalidatePath` from a mutation — this is the one place in the product where time-based revalidation may be unavoidable, and CLAUDE.md's blanket prohibition should be revisited *for this case specifically*).

**Adopt only** the hours line and the "Now" badge treatment, with the value derived server-side at prerender.

---

### MENU-10 — *An owner or staff member can toggle an item as available / sold-out, and it reflects to diners quickly* → **partial**

**What holds — fully, and it is the right design.** Sold-out items (`out: true` on `i7`) **stay listed**, carry a neutral-tone `Badge` ("Sold out" / "Elfogyott" / "Epuizat"), remain tappable, and the sheet renders `t.soldOutNote`: *"Gone for tonight. Your server can suggest something close."* That is precisely the calm, actionable treatment the voice register calls for — it says what happened and what to do — and hiding sold-out items would be worse (a diner who came for that dish learns nothing). Adopt as-is, including the note.

**What does not.** The owner/staff toggle, and "reflects to diners quickly" — which is the `revalidatePath` invalidation path. Both out of a template's scope. Note that MENU-10 names **staff** as an actor, which lands on `.claude/CLAUDE.md`'s explicit warning that column-level "staff can only edit availability" must be enforced by a `SECURITY DEFINER` RPC, not by RLS row policies plus UI restriction.

**One inconsistency to fix on adoption:** the sold-out badge is `tone="neutral"` on the row but the note in the sheet sits on `--surface-sunken`. Both are correctly *quiet*, which is right — a sold-out dish is information, not an error.

---

### LANG-05 — *A diner's language is auto-detected from their browser when they open the menu* → **partial** *(policy holds, mechanism does not)*

**What holds — the detection policy, and it is well judged.** `lang()` (lines 334–341): consult an explicit user override first, then an explicit prop, then iterate `navigator.languages` **in order** (falling back to `[navigator.language]`), normalise each to its 2-char prefix lowercased, return the first that is in the supported set, else `'en'`. Ordered-preference matching rather than first-tag-only is the correct behaviour and is frequently got wrong. Paired with `t.detected` — *"Set from your phone's language. Change it whenever you like."* — which is a genuinely good disclosure line and should become a Copywriting Contract row.

**What does not — the mechanism, and this is architectural.** `navigator` exists only in the browser. CLAUDE.md mandates a prerendered, CDN-edge-served diner page with **zero database round-trip on the request path**, and lists "client-rendered SPA fetching menu data on mount" under *What NOT to Use*. Reading `navigator.languages` on first paint gives you one of two bad outcomes:

1. The page prerenders in some default language and swaps after hydration → a visible flash of the **entire menu** in the wrong language, on exactly the poor mobile connection DINE-03 is about; or
2. The page becomes client-rendered → forbidden.

**Recommended mechanism — see `## Pattern 9`.** One static page per (venue, language) at `/menu/[slug]/[lang]`, with `Accept-Language` negotiation done as a redirect in `proxy.ts` (Next 16's renamed middleware), which runs *before* the cache and therefore does not de-optimise the destination. Every rendered page stays fully static; only a 307 sits on the detection path. The template's matching *policy* ports over directly — it is the same algorithm, run against the `Accept-Language` header instead of `navigator.languages`.

---

### LANG-06 — *A diner can manually switch the menu language* → **partial**

**What holds.** Three pills HU/EN/RO rendered as `Button size="lg"` (`hint-size="56px,48px"` → **48px tall, comfortably over the 44px floor**), the current language as `variant="primary"` and the others `secondary`, and the override taking precedence over both prop and detection because `lang()` checks `this.state.lang` first. Placement — immediately under the venue name, above the fold, adjacent to the `t.detected` disclosure — is right.

**What does not.**

1. **Persistence.** `this.state.lang` is in-memory. The README says the pills "override the detection for the rest of the visit"; across a reload, a back-navigation, or the very common case of a diner backgrounding the browser and returning, the override is gone and detection re-runs. **The claim does not hold.**
2. **Labels are 2-letter codes only.** A diner who cannot read the currently-rendered language has to decode "HU/EN/RO". The convention for language switchers is the *endonym* — Magyar / English / Română — which the template already has in `SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES`-equivalent data but does not use here.
3. **No group semantics.** Three loose buttons: no `role="group"`, no group label, no `aria-pressed` or `aria-current` on the active one. A screen reader gets three unlabelled two-letter buttons.

**Recommended fix, which is the same fix as LANG-05.** Make the pills **links to `/menu/[slug]/[lang]`**. Then "for the rest of the visit" is carried by the URL — surviving reload, back/forward, and sharing — with **zero storage, zero cookie, zero consent question** (which matters: CLAUDE.md's "no consent banner, ever" makes even a functional cookie a conversation, though a language-preference cookie would be consent-exempt as strictly-necessary under ePrivacy Art. 5(3)), and zero dynamic rendering. It is strictly better than the template's in-memory state on every axis.

---

### THEME-03 — *Every template renders as intentional and attractive with zero item photos, some photos, or a full set* → **partial**

**⚠ This verdict corrects a factual premise in CONTEXT.md D-08.**

CONTEXT.md D-08 states the imported template "currently renders every image as a 'labelled striped placeholder' while simultaneously claiming the zero-photo state is 'the design's default, not a degraded mode'", and calls those two claims inconsistent. **Reading the source, they are not inconsistent — the README is just imprecise.** With `photos: 'none'`:

- `showCover` is `false` (line 434) → the cover block does not render.
- `wantsPhoto()` returns `false` unconditionally (lines 350–355) → neither the 68px row thumb (line 116) nor the 186px sheet image (line 142) renders.

**No placeholder renders in the zero-photo state.** The striped placeholders exist only in the `some`/`full` states, where a real photo would go. **D-08's "no image slot at all — not a wash, not a stripe, nothing occupying where a photo would be" is already satisfied.**

**But D-08's design conclusion still stands, for a different reason.** D-08 also requires "a genuinely different, typographic layout… generous spacing." The template's zero-photo state is the photo layout **minus the photo**, not a different layout:

| Property | photos: some/full | photos: none |
|---|---|---|
| Row min-height | 64px | 64px |
| Row padding | `14px 18px` | `14px 18px` |
| Dish name | `--font-display` 17px/1.25 | identical |
| Right column | `flex-column`, `gap:9px`: price + 68px thumb | same column, price only |
| Section heading, rules, type scale | — | identical |

Nothing compensates. The right column simply collapses to the price and the left column reflows wider. PROJECT.md's reason for D-08 — "empty image slots look worse than a design that never expected them" — is satisfied on the *slot*; it is not satisfied on the *design that never expected them*.

**What holds:** the three-state architecture. One `photos` mode driving cover + row + sheet coherently, with `some` keyed off per-item data, is exactly what THEME-03 asks a template to demonstrate, and it is the right shape.

**What does not:** the zero-photo state as a *design*, and — less obviously but more importantly — **the `some` state is unsolved**. `wantsPhoto()` in `some` mode returns `Boolean(item.photo)`, so rows alternate between having and not having a 68px thumb, producing a ragged right edge with nothing reconciling it. THEME-03 names "some photos" explicitly, and it is the hardest of the three to make look intentional. The template does not attempt it.

**Recommendation for the plan.** Correct D-08's factual premise in CONTEXT.md (or note the correction in the plan so a later reader is not misled), keep its design conclusion, and **add the `some` state as named work** — it is currently invisible in both CONTEXT.md and the ROADMAP, and it is the state most real venues will land in.

---

### ACCT-02 — *An owner can create a venue and set its name, currency (RON/HUF/EUR), and enabled languages* → **partial** *(weakest claim in the table)*

**Category error again.** ACCT-02 is an owner requirement, and **Phase 01 already shipped it** (`components/venue-form.tsx`). The template covers none of the owner surface — and the one leg of ACCT-02 that is *currently broken* is EUR venue creation (**G-01-13**), which this phase fixes and which the template has nothing to do with.

**What genuinely transfers: the per-currency display convention.** `money()` (lines 343–348) formats:

| Currency | Template output (7900 HUF base) | Convention |
|---|---|---|
| HUF | `"7 900 Ft"` | zero decimals, space grouping, `Ft` postfix |
| RON | `"101,28 lei"` | 2 decimals, comma decimal, `lei` postfix |
| EUR | `"20,26 €"` | 2 decimals, comma decimal, `€` postfix |

**This resolves audit warning W-3.** The design project's `readme.md` mandates "Continental decimal comma for currency; €148,50" as a *global* rule, which is wrong for zero-decimal HUF. The template contradicts its own readme, and **the template is right**. Carry the per-currency convention forward and correct the readme rule alongside D-11.

**What does not transfer.**

1. **The FX conversion is demo scaffolding.** Rates are hardcoded (`huf/78`, `huf/390`) and the README concedes real venues store one currency each. Prices are authored in HUF and converted purely so one dataset can demo three markets. Do not port `money()`'s conversion.
2. **HUF is rounded to the nearest 10 inside the formatter** (`Math.round(huf/10)*10`). That is a display decision baked into a formatting function and would silently corrupt an authored price.
3. **No thousands grouping for RON/EUR.** `(huf/78).toFixed(2)` never groups, so a 7 900 lei price renders `"7900,00 lei"` — wrong for ro-RO, which groups with `.`.

**Recommendation: use `Intl.NumberFormat`, not a hand-rolled formatter.** Verified on this machine (Node 24.14.1, ICU 78.2):

| Call | Output |
|---|---|
| `Intl.NumberFormat('hu-HU',{style:'currency',currency:'HUF'}).format(148500)` | `"148 500 Ft"` ✓ |
| `…format(7900)` | `"7900 Ft"` — **note: no grouping at 4 digits** (ICU `minimumGroupingDigits` for hu-HU), where the template emits `"7 900 Ft"` |
| `Intl.NumberFormat('ro-RO',{style:'currency',currency:'RON',currencyDisplay:'narrowSymbol'}).format(1903.85)` | `"1.903,85 lei"` ✓ — correct grouping the template lacks |
| `…currencyDisplay:'symbol'` (default) | `"1.903,85 RON"` — **`narrowSymbol` is required to get "lei"** |
| `Intl.NumberFormat('de-DE',{style:'currency',currency:'EUR'}).format(20.26)` | `"20,26 €"` ✓ |

Two gotchas the plan should pin: `currencyDisplay:'narrowSymbol'` is required for RON to render as `lei` rather than `RON`; and the 4-digit HUF grouping difference is a real, visible divergence from the template that should be a deliberate choice, not a surprise. Both are worth a unit test with literal expected strings, since ICU data can shift between Node majors.

---

### Cross-cutting: the template is a spec, not code

`QrMenu.dc.html` is authored in the design project's own runtime — `<x-dc>`, `<sc-if>`, `<sc-for>`, `<x-import component-from-global-scope="CenaDesignSystem_07b799.Button">` — with **inline `style=` attributes throughout and not one Tailwind class**. It also uses non-standard attributes (`style-hover`, `hint-size`, `hint-placeholder-val`) that exist only in that runtime.

**The plan must state explicitly that this file is re-implemented, never ported.** Concretely, on re-implementation: every `<sc-if>` becomes a conditional render, every `<sc-for>` a `.map()`, every `x-import` a repo primitive, and every inline `style=` a Tailwind utility resolving to the same semantic token. The sheet becomes a Radix `Dialog`, the language pills become links, and `renderVals()`'s derivations move to the Server Component.

**The one thing worth extracting verbatim: the `T` string tables.** Three complete, idiomatic HU/EN/RO string sets written in the house voice, including the allergen disclaimer, the sold-out note, the empty-filter state and the pluralised count line. That is real translation work already done, and it should be lifted into `lib/copy.ts` (or its diner-side equivalent) rather than re-authored — after the D-04 register pass and with the DINE-04 string replaced per D-07.

## Architectural Responsibility Map

| Capability | Primary Tier | Secondary Tier | Rationale |
|------------|-------------|----------------|-----------|
| Cena design tokens (colour/type/spacing/shape/motion) | CDN / Static (compiled CSS) | — | Tailwind v4 compiles `@theme` at build; tokens are bytes in a stylesheet, never runtime state |
| Self-hosted typefaces | CDN / Static | Frontend Server (build) | `next/font/google` downloads at build; browser fetches from own origin |
| Re-skinned Radix primitives | Browser / Client | Frontend Server (SSR) | Radix behaviour is client-side; the markup is server-rendered |
| Venue theme token values | Frontend Server (prerender) | Database (source of truth) | Values must be **baked into the prerendered HTML** — a request-time DB read violates CLAUDE.md's zero-round-trip rule |
| Venue theme → CSS variable injection | Frontend Server (RSC `style` prop) | — | Not Browser: a client-side theme apply causes FOUC and a hydration round-trip on the diner critical path |
| WCAG contrast guardrail | API / Backend (write gate) | Build/test (sweep) | The rule must hold for *any* caller, so it belongs on the write path (Zod), with a test-time exhaustive sweep as the SC4 proof |
| Venue theme invalidation | Frontend Server (`revalidatePath`) | — | On-demand, from the owner's mutation, per CLAUDE.md |
| Copy deck (`lib/copy.ts`) | Frontend Server | — | Server Components render it; no client bundle cost |
| Dark-mode token definitions | CDN / Static (dormant) | — | D-10: defined, never selected; zero runtime tier |

### Supporting — add only if a specific decision demands it

| Library | Version | Purpose | When to Use |
|---------|---------|---------|-------------|
| `culori` | 4.x (latest 2025-06-27, 1.67M/wk) | oklch↔sRGB conversion + `wcagContrast()` | **Only if** any *venue-controllable* token is expressed in `oklch`. If the venue contract is hex-only (recommended), skip it. |
| `fonttools` (`pyftsubset`) | Python | Custom unicode-range subsetting | **Not recommended** — see § Don't Hand-Roll. Would also raise an OFL Reserved Font Name question for IBM Plex Mono. |
| `@axe-core/playwright` | latest | Rendered-DOM a11y sweep | Only if the planner wants a rendered SC3/SC4 check; the repo has no e2e harness in the vitest suite today |

### Alternatives Considered

| Instead of | Could Use | Tradeoff |
|------------|-----------|----------|
| `next/font/google` for the Cena pairing | `next/font/local` + committed `.woff2` subsets | Local wins on build-time network independence and byte size (~40% smaller than Google's `latin-ext`); loses automatic `size-adjust` fallback metrics, automatic per-subset `unicode-range`, and reproducibility (binary blobs in git). **Also raises OFL §5 for IBM Plex Mono ("Plex" is a Reserved Font Name) — a self-produced subset is a Modified Version.** Recommend `next/font/google`. |
| Hand-rolled WCAG 2.1 relative-luminance function | `wcag-contrast` (113k/wk, OK) or `culori` | The formula is ~15 normative lines. A dependency inside a *legal release gate* (THEME-04) is a supply-chain surface for no gain — unless oklch parsing is needed, in which case `culori`. |
| WCAG 2.1 contrast ratio | APCA (`apca-w3`, 57k/wk, OK) | APCA is perceptually better but is **not** WCAG 2.x and **SC4 names "WCAG AA 4.5:1" explicitly**. Deviating would make the success criterion unfalsifiable. Use WCAG 2.1 as normative; record APCA Lc as advisory only if desired. |
| `radix-nova` `select` primitive | keep the raw `<select>` currently in `venue-form.tsx` | Raw `<select>` is the *better* mobile control (native picker, one-handed) and `native-select` exists in the registry for exactly this. The DS's `Select` is a styled listbox. **SC3 ("usable one-handed on a phone") argues for keeping native.** Flag as a design decision, not a mechanical swap. |
| `shadcn add toast` | keep `sonner` | `toast` has **no** `radix-nova` variant (verified 404). `sonner` is already wired into `app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx` and `UI-SPEC E11`. Keep it. |

**Installation** (the only install this phase needs):

```bash
pnpm exec shadcn add select radio-group switch field tabs tooltip
# `field` pulls `label` + `separator` as registry dependencies.
# `label` ALREADY EXISTS at components/ui/label.tsx — do not let the CLI overwrite it silently.
```

**Version verification:** `pnpm --version` → **10.18.2**; `node --version` → **v24.14.1**; `pnpm exec tsc --version` → **5.9.3**. Registry items fetched live from `https://ui.shadcn.com/r/styles/radix-nova/<name>.json` this session.

## Package Legitimacy Audit

This phase installs **no new npm package**. The only additions are shadcn registry *source files*, which are copied into `components/ui/` and become repo code — not dependencies. The table below covers the optional libraries named in § Supporting, run through `gsd-tools query package-legitimacy check --ecosystem npm`:

| Package | Registry | Latest publish | Downloads | Source Repo | Verdict | Disposition |
|---------|----------|-----|-----------|-------------|---------|-------------|
| `wcag-contrast` | npm | 2019-11-05 | 113,488/wk | github.com/tmcw/wcag-contrast | **OK** | Optional — not recommended (hand-roll the 15-line formula instead) |
| `culori` | npm | 2025-06-27 | 1,670,050/wk | github.com/Evercoder/culori | **OK** | Optional — devDependency only, and only if oklch parsing is needed |
| `colorjs.io` | npm | 2026-07-24 | 7,276,823/wk | github.com/color-js/color.js | **SUS** (`too-new`) | Not recommended. **The `too-new` flag is a false positive** — the seam reads *latest* publish date, and 7.2M weekly downloads on a mature library contradicts it. Rejected on merit (heavyweight), not on the flag. |
| `apca-w3` | npm | 2022-07-04 | 57,427/wk | github.com/Myndex/apca-w3 | **OK** | Not recommended — SC4 names WCAG 2.1, not APCA |
| `chroma-js` | npm | — | — | — | OK | Not recommended — superseded by culori for this job |

**Packages removed due to [SLOP] verdict:** none.
**Packages flagged as suspicious [SUS]:** `colorjs.io` — and it is not being recommended anyway. If the planner overrides and adopts it, a `checkpoint:human-verify` is required before install.

`fonttools` / `pyftsubset` (PyPI) was **not** legitimacy-checked because it is not recommended; if the planner takes the custom-subsetting fork, it must be checked on **PyPI**, not npm.

### Component Responsibilities

| File | Responsibility after 01.1 |
|---|---|
| `app/globals.css` | The single Tailwind entry. Grows `@import` lines for the token files at the very top, keeps its `@theme inline` block, keeps the `--max-width-*`/`--min-width-*` shields |
| `app/tokens/cena.css` *(new)* | Cena product-brand ramps + semantic tokens (`@theme inline`) |
| `app/tokens/venue.css` *(new)* | The venue-themable contract: fallback values only. **No Cena hue appears here** |
| `app/layout.tsx` | Declares the three `next/font/google` families, exposes them as `--font-serif` / `--font-sans` / `--font-mono` |
| `components/ui/*` | 11 re-skinned + 7 added (6 named + `separator`) |
| `lib/theme/contrast.ts` *(new)* | `contrastRatio()` — pure, dependency-free, WCAG 2.1 |
| `lib/theme/venue-tokens.ts` *(new)* | The venue token *contract* (which names exist, which pairs must hold) + `resolveVenueTheme()` |
| `lib/copy.ts` | Absorbs the D-04 lexicon re-cut and the D-07 last-good string |
| `components/venue-form.tsx` | Re-skinned **and** G-01-13 fixed |
| `actions/venues.ts` | G-01-14 fixed (`revalidatePath` before `redirect`) |
| `.planning/design-archive/` *(new)* | D-12 archive — 9 files pulled from the design project |

### Recommended Project Structure

```
app/
├── globals.css              # entry: @import tailwindcss, then tokens, then @theme inline
├── tokens/

lib/theme/
├── contrast.ts              # contrastRatio() — pure WCAG 2.1

components/ui/               # 11 re-skinned + select, radio-group, switch, field, tabs, tooltip, separator
tests/theme/
```

### Pattern 1 — Self-hosting and subsetting the Cena pairing (SC1, D-03, D-09)

**What:** Declare all three families with `next/font/google`, restricted to `latin` + `latin-ext`. Do **not** build a custom subsetting pipeline.

**Why this is correct, evidenced rather than asserted:**

1. **`next/font/google` self-hosts.** *"CSS and font files are downloaded during the build process and self-hosted alongside your other static assets. This means that no requests are sent to Google by the browser at runtime."* `[CITED: nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/components/font]`
2. **Empirically true in this repo already.** I grepped the existing build output: `.next/static/chunks/*.css` contains **zero** `https?://` matches, and all seven `url()` references point at `../media/*.woff2`. `[VERIFIED: repo build output, this session]`
3. **`latin-ext` provably covers every RO and HU diacritic** for all three families. Verified codepoint-by-codepoint against Google's own metadata API (`fonts.google.com/metadata/fonts/<Family>`), not assumed:

| Glyph | Codepoint | Newsreader | Instrument Sans | IBM Plex Mono |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ă` / `Ă` | 259 / 258 | `latin-ext` 256–304 ✓ | `latin-ext` 256–263 ✓ | `latin-ext` 256–304 ✓ |
| `â` / `Â` | 226 / 194 | `latin` 160–255 ✓ | `latin` 191–255 ✓ | `latin` 160–255 ✓ |
| `î` / `Î` | 238 / 206 | `latin` ✓ | `latin` ✓ | `latin` ✓ |
| `ș` / `Ș` | 537 / 536 | `latin-ext` 506–539 ✓ | `latin-ext` 536–539 ✓ | `latin-ext` 536–539 ✓ |
| `ț` / `Ț` | 539 / 538 | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `ő` / `Ő` | 337 / 336 | `latin-ext` 330–337 ✓ | `latin-ext` 336–337 ✓ | `latin-ext` 306–337 ✓ |
| `ű` / `Ű` | 369 / 368 | `latin-ext` 340–382 ✓ | `latin-ext` 362–382 ✓ | `latin-ext` 340–383 ✓ |

   `[VERIFIED: fonts.google.com/metadata/fonts, 2026-08-04]` — **100% coverage, no gaps, for all three families.**

4. **Licences confirmed, not assumed** `[VERIFIED: raw.githubusercontent.com/google/fonts/main/ofl/*/METADATA.pb and OFL.txt]`:

| Family | Licence | Reserved Font Name | Variable? | Axes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Newsreader | **OFL 1.1** | **none** | yes | `opsz`, `wght` |
| Instrument Sans | **OFL 1.1** | **none** | yes | `wdth`, `wght` |
| IBM Plex Mono | **OFL 1.1** | **"Plex"** ⚠ | **no** | — (static weights) |

   Two consequences the planner must absorb. **(a)** IBM Plex Mono is *not* a variable font, so `next/font/google` **requires an explicit `weight` array** — omitting it is a build error, not a silent default. **(b)** IBM Plex Mono's Reserved Font Name means a *self-produced* subset is an OFL "Modified Version" that may not carry the "Plex" name. Shipping Google's own official `latin-ext` build through `next/font` sidesteps this entirely; a `pyftsubset` pipeline does not.

**The committed-subsets-vs-build-step fork, decided:**

| | `next/font/google` (**recommended**) | `next/font/local` + committed `pyftsubset` output |
|---|---|---|
| Bytes | Google's `latin-ext` per family/weight | ~30–45% smaller (RO/HU-only range) |
| Build tooling | none | Python + fonttools in the build, or checked-in binaries regenerated by hand |
| Fallback metrics (`size-adjust`, CLS) | automatic | must be hand-computed |
| `unicode-range` splitting | automatic per subset | must be hand-authored |
| Reproducibility | deterministic from source | binary blobs in git, no provenance |
| OFL RFN exposure (IBM Plex Mono) | none | **real** |
| Build-time network | needs `fonts.gstatic.com` at build (cached in `.next/cache/fonts`) | none |
| Repo precedent | **already the pattern** (`Inter` in `app/layout.tsx`) | none |
| Environment today | works now | `pyftsubset: no`, `fontTools: not installed` (verified) |

**Recommendation:** `next/font/google`. Revisit only if a *measured* diner-page font budget fails DINE-03 — and make that a Phase 2 measurement, not a Phase 01.1 assumption. Record the byte cost in the plan so the measurement has a baseline.

**🚫 `tokens/fonts.css` MUST NOT be migrated. This is a one-line instruction the plan has to carry explicitly.**

The design system's font layer is three lines, quoted verbatim from the live project `[VERIFIED: DesignSync mirror, README-MIRROR.md]`:

```css
/* Cena webfonts.
   NOTE: no font binaries were provided with the brief. These are the nearest
   Google Fonts matches to the intended voice and are loaded from Google's CDN.
   Swap the @import for local @font-face rules when licensed files arrive. */
@import url('https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Newsreader:ital,opsz,wght@0,6..72,300..700;1,6..72,300..700&family=Instrument+Sans:ital,wght@0,400..700;1,400..700&family=IBM+Plex+Mono:wght@400;500;600&display=swap');
```

**An instruction to "adopt `tokens/*.css`", read literally, regresses SC1 on its own** — this single file reintroduces the exact third-party font request SC1 forbids and W-2 flagged. The design system's own comment anticipates the swap ("Swap the `@import` for local `@font-face` rules"), and `next/font/google` *is* that swap, done better.

Three details worth harvesting from that `@import` before discarding the file, because they encode the DS's actual type intent:

| Family | DS request | Maps to |
|---|---|---|
| Newsreader | `ital,opsz,wght@0,6..72,300..700;1,6..72,300..700` | roman **and italic**, optical size 6–72, weights 300–700. The template uses italic (`font-style:italic` at line 34), so **italic must be requested** — `next/font/google` needs `style: ["normal","italic"]` |
| Instrument Sans | `ital,wght@0,400..700;1,400..700` | roman + italic, 400–700 |
| IBM Plex Mono | `wght@400;500;600` | three static weights — confirms the explicit `weight` array required for this non-variable family |

Requesting italic doubles the file count per family per subset. Since the diner surface uses italic in exactly one place (the venue's descriptive aside), the plan should decide deliberately whether to ship italic or restyle that line — this is a real byte-budget decision on the DINE-03 critical path, not a detail.

**Warning the planner must carry:** `.design-sync/fonts/inter-*.woff2` are **committed copies harvested from `.next/static/media`**, and `.design-sync/NOTES.md` states explicitly that *"if the app ever changes font or weights, `fonts/inter.css` will not follow automatically."* Changing the app's fonts therefore breaks the design-sync preview bundle silently. It also invalidates `.design-sync/tailwind-entry.css`, which **defines `--font-sans` for the out-of-Next preview context** — leaving it stale renders every preview in browser-default serif.

### Pattern 2 — The Cena/venue token contract in Tailwind v4 (SC4, D-02)

**What:** Two `@theme inline` layers with a hard naming boundary, and a per-venue value injected as a `style` prop on the diner page's root Server Component.

**`@theme inline` is not optional here — it is the mechanism.** Tailwind's docs give the exact reason: `@theme inline { --font-sans: var(--font-inter) }` compiles to `.font-sans { font-family: var(--font-inter) }`, i.e. the *utility emits the inner variable reference*. Without `inline`, the utility emits `var(--color-x)` where `--color-x: var(--venue-ink)` is resolved **in `:root`'s scope**, so a nested override of `--venue-ink` is ignored — Tailwind documents this as the scope-resolution failure `inline` exists to fix. `[CITED: tailwindcss.com/docs/theme#referencing-other-variables]`

Nested-scope resolution is exactly what a per-venue theme needs, so **every venue-themable token must be declared inside `@theme inline`.** The repo already uses this idiom (`--font-sans: var(--font-sans)` in `app/globals.css`), so it is a continuation, not a new concept.

**The naming boundary — this is the D-02 contract:**

| Layer | Prefix | Who sets it | May appear on diner surface? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cena product brand | `--szeged-* --napfeny-* --paprika-* --tisza-*` | Cena, fixed | **NO** (D-02) |
| Cena structure (brand-agnostic) | `--spacing-* --radius-* --text-* --ease-* --duration-*` | Cena, fixed | **YES — and immutable by the venue** |
| Venue skin | `--venue-*` | the venue, within guardrails | **YES — this is the only thing that varies** |

Layout, spacing, type *scale*, radii and motion are Cena-fixed on both surfaces. Only `--venue-ink`, `--venue-paper`, `--venue-surface`, `--venue-accent`, `--venue-accent-ink`, `--venue-muted-ink`, `--venue-rule`, `--font-venue-display`, `--font-venue-body` vary. That set is small on purpose: PROJECT.md excludes deep per-venue customisation because "restaurants would make ugly menus, and visual quality is the differentiator."

**How the venue's values reach CSS without a request-path DB read.** This interacts hard with CLAUDE.md's ISR/CDN mandate. Ranked:

1. **`style` prop on the diner page's root Server Component — recommended.**
   The `/menu/[slug]` page is prerendered per venue. The venue's token values are read from Supabase **at prerender time** and emitted as inline custom properties in the static HTML. Zero request-path DB read, zero extra network request, zero FOUC, no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, and React escapes the attribute value. Theme changes invalidate via `revalidatePath('/menu/' + slug)` from the owner's mutation — precisely the on-demand pattern CLAUDE.md mandates. It also inherits ISR's last-good-serve behaviour for free, which is what DINE-04 depends on.
2. `<style>` block with `:root`-scoped overrides — same timing, but reintroduces a string-interpolation injection surface for no benefit. Reject.
3. Middleware / `proxy.ts` rewriting a theme class — forces the route dynamic. Reject.
4. Client-side fetch-and-apply — explicitly listed under CLAUDE.md's *What NOT to Use*. Reject.

**Font pairings must be a closed set of statically-declared `next/font` instances**, selected by class name (`theme-pairing-a`, …). A dynamic font family name cannot work: `next/font` resolves at build time. This is the mechanical reason D-03's "small curated set" is the only implementable shape, and worth stating in the plan so Phase 4 does not rediscover it.

**Hex-only rule.** Constrain every *venue-controllable* colour to sRGB hex (`#rrggbb`). It is what a colour picker produces, it is what WCAG 2.1's relative-luminance formula is defined over, and it removes the need for an oklch parsing dependency inside a legal release gate. Cena's *own* tokens may stay in whatever the DS ships.

#### The actual token vocabulary the diner surface consumes

This is no longer guesswork. Extracting every `var(--…)` from `QrMenu.dc.html` gives the exact semantic surface the venue contract must cover — **45 distinct tokens**, with usage counts `[VERIFIED: mirror, this session]`:

| Family | Tokens (usage count) | Venue-themable? |
|---|---|---|
| **Text** | `--text-subtle` (14), `--text-heading` (10), `--text-body` (6), `--text-muted` (5), `--text-on-accent` (1), `--text-link` (1) | **YES** — these are the ink layer |
| **Surface** | `--surface-sunken` (7), `--surface-card` (3), `--surface-hover` (3), `--surface-selected` (1), `--surface-overlay` (1) | **YES** — the paper layer |
| **Accent** | `--accent` (3), `--accent-soft` (3), `--accent-text-on-soft` (4), `--border-accent` (2) | **YES** — the venue's brand colour |
| **Border** | `--border-subtle` (6), `--border-default` (3), `--border-strong` (1) | **YES** (3:1 non-text threshold) |
| **Status** | `--warning-soft`, `--warning-border`, `--warning-text` (1 each) | **⚠ UNDECIDED — see below** |
| **Type scale** | `--text-2xs` (5), `--text-xs` (4), `--text-sm` (4), `--text-base` (6), `--text-md` (2), `--text-lg` (2), `--text-xl` (1) | **NO — Cena-fixed** (D-02: type *scale* stays fixed) |
| **Composite type** | `--type-label` (8), `--type-eyebrow` (3), `--tracking-caps` (3) | **NO — Cena-fixed** |
| **Font family** | `--font-display` (7), `--font-mono` (10), `--font-sans` (1) | **YES** — D-03's pairing varies these |
| **Shape** | `--radius-md` (5), `--radius-sheet` (4), `--radius-full` (4), `--radius-xs` (3) | **NO — Cena-fixed** |
| **Motion** | `--transition-control` (6), `--ease-out-soft` (2), `--duration-base`, `--duration-slow` | **NO — Cena-fixed** |
| **Elevation** | `--shadow-sm`, `--shadow-xl` | **NO — Cena-fixed** |
| **RAW RAMP** ⚠ | `--tisza-200` (3), `--tisza-100` (2) | **NEITHER — this is a leak** |

Three findings fall straight out of this table, and each is actionable.

**(1) `--tisza-100` / `--tisza-200` are a raw-ramp leak into the diner surface.** They set the page background outside the 520px column (line 15) and the striped placeholder pattern (lines 26, 117, 143). `tisza` is Cena's *neutral* ramp, so this is not a breach of D-02's letter (D-02 forbids *azure*), but it is exactly the structural failure the contract must prevent: **the diner surface must consume only semantic names, never ramp names**, or a venue theme can never re-map them. On a venue with a warm paper colour, a cool tisza page background is a visible seam. **This is what the SC4/D-02 token-boundary test should assert: no `--szeged-*`, `--napfeny-*`, `--paprika-*` or `--tisza-*` identifier may appear in any diner-surface file.** That gives the test a real, greppable rule instead of an aspirational one.

**(2) The accent family is the venue's, and one usage may already violate D-02.** `--accent` / `--accent-soft` / `--accent-text-on-soft` / `--text-on-accent` / `--border-accent` / `--surface-selected` drive the active category chip, dietary chips, the active dietary filter, the active variant row and the section underline. Under D-02 every one of these must resolve to the **venue's** accent. But the language pills use `Button variant="primary"` (line 37), and in the DS `Button`'s primary is Cena's azure fill. **Verify against `components/Button` before adopting**; the safe rule for the plan is that on the diner surface `Button variant="primary"` must take its fill from `--accent`, not from a szeged ramp token.

**(3) The status family is under-specified by D-02, and it appears on the diner surface twice.** The "Now" badge is `Badge tone="warning"` — the README calls it "the one gold element per screen, per the napfeny rule" — and the DINE-04 offline banner uses `--warning-soft`/`-border`/`-text`. So **Cena's napfeny gold renders on a venue-branded menu**, which is the same class of clash D-02's own rationale names ("Cena chrome in azure would clash with any venue whose brand is red"). D-02 does not say. **Recommendation: keep status colours Cena-fixed on the diner surface, and say so explicitly in the contract.** A warning that reads as a warning is a safety affordance — sold-out, allergen, stale-menu — and letting a venue theme it is how a venue accidentally makes a warning invisible. But because they sit on venue-controlled paper, **every status pair must be in the SC4 contrast set.** Flag to the user as an open decision (see `## Open Questions`).

**(4) `--type-label` and `--type-eyebrow` are CSS `font:` shorthands** (`font:var(--type-label)`), not individual properties. Tailwind v4 has no theme namespace for the `font` shorthand, so these cannot become utilities directly — they must either decompose into `--text-*` + `--font-weight-*` + `--tracking-*` triples, or ship as `@utility` definitions. A small mechanical detail that will otherwise surface as a surprise in Wave 1.

### Pattern 3 — The THEME-04 contrast guardrail (SC4 — the mechanism CONTEXT.md deferred to research)

**What:** Three artifacts, all authored in 01.1, none consumed until Phase 4.

**(a) `contrastRatio(fg, bg): number` — pure, dependency-free, WCAG 2.1.**
The normative formula: linearise each sRGB channel (`c ≤ 0.04045 ? c/12.92 : ((c+0.055)/1.055)^2.4`), `L = 0.2126R + 0.7152G + 0.0722B`, ratio `= (Llighter + 0.05) / (Ldarker + 0.05)`. ~15 lines. **Do not take a dependency for this** — see § Don't Hand-Roll for why this is the one exception to that section's usual direction.

**Algorithm choice, justified:** SC4 names "WCAG AA 4.5:1". WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.3 is what defines that number. APCA is perceptually superior and is the WCAG 3 *draft* direction, but adopting it would mean SC4's own threshold no longer means anything measurable — an APCA Lc value is not a ratio. **Use WCAG 2.1 as the normative gate.** If the team wants APCA, record it as an advisory second column, never as the pass/fail.

**(b) `resolveVenueTheme(input: VenueThemeInput): VenueTokens` — a total function that structurally cannot return a failing set.**
The venue supplies few inputs (brand colour, paper/ink polarity, pairing id). The resolver *derives* every text token by picking, from a fixed ink/paper candidate pair, whichever reaches the higher ratio against each surface. It returns `{ ok: true, tokens }` or `{ ok: false, failures: Pair[] }` — never a silently-bad set. This is the shape that matters most, because it makes the guardrail a property of the *type*, not of a validation step someone can forget to call.

**(c) `CONTRAST_PAIRS` — an explicit adjacency list, not a cartesian product.**
A cartesian sweep would assert nonsense (accent-ink on paper never co-occurs). Enumerate only pairs that can actually render together. **The list below is no longer invented — every pair is a real co-occurrence read out of `QrMenu.dc.html`, with the line it renders at:**

| # | Foreground | Background | Threshold | Renders at | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `--text-body` | `--surface-card` | 4.5:1 | 15, 21, 68 | body copy |
| 2 | `--text-heading` | `--surface-card` | 4.5:1 | 33, 94, 99, 115, 150 | dish names, section headings, prices |
| 3 | `--text-muted` | `--surface-card` | 4.5:1 | 34, 104, 151 | descriptions — **muted is where AA usually breaks** |
| 4 | `--text-subtle` | `--surface-card` | 4.5:1 | 41, 53, 90 | detected-language line, service hours, count line — **at `--text-xs`/10px, the smallest type on the surface** |
| 5 | **`--text-subtle`** | **`--surface-sunken`** | **4.5:1** | 110, 133, 134, 194 | **allergen chips (DINE-06), the VAT line, the nutrition tile labels, the footer.** Lowest-contrast token on the *second*-lightest surface, at `--text-2xs`. **This is the pair most likely to fail, and it carries the allergen display** |
| 6 | `--text-on-accent` | `--accent` | 4.5:1 | 65 | active category chip |
| 7 | `--accent-text-on-soft` | `--accent-soft` | 4.5:1 | 75, 107, 206 | active dietary filter, dietary chips |
| 8 | `--accent-text-on-soft` | `--surface-selected` | 4.5:1 | 166 | selected variant row |
| 9 | `--text-link` | `--surface-card` | 4.5:1 | 83 | "Clear filters" |
| 10 | `--text-body` | `--surface-hover` | 4.5:1 | 68, 79, 96 | hovered rows |
| 11 | **`--warning-text`** | **`--warning-soft`** | **4.5:1** | **19–21** | **the DINE-04 last-good banner — a release gate** |
| 12 | `--text-heading` | `--surface-sunken` | 4.5:1 | 193 | nutrition values |
| 13 | `--text-body` | `--surface-sunken` | 4.5:1 | 157 | the sold-out note (MENU-10) |
| 14 | `--border-subtle` | `--surface-card` | **3:1** | 26, 44, 61, 96, 132, 182 | non-text (WCAG 1.4.11) — **a different threshold; asserting 4.5 here produces a false failure** |
| 15 | `--border-default` | `--surface-card` | **3:1** | 68, 79, 172 | idle chip and variant borders |
| 16 | `--border-accent` | `--surface-card` | **3:1** | 75, 166 | selected-state borders |
| 17 | `--warning-border` | `--warning-soft` | **3:1** | 19 | banner rule |
| 18 | unverified-field marker ink | its background | 4.5:1 | *(net-new)* | **INGEST-06 marking (D-06) — a legal release gate, absent from the template** |

**Row 5 is the finding.** `--text-subtle` on `--surface-sunken` at `--text-2xs` is simultaneously the lowest-contrast token pair, the smallest type size, and the surface that carries **allergen chips**. It is the single most likely AA failure on the whole diner surface and the one with the worst consequence. Rows 11 and 18 sit on release gates. Rows 14–17 are the ones that produce false failures if 4.5:1 is applied uniformly.

**A second finding from the same extraction:** `--text-subtle` is used **14 times** — more than any other token — and always at 10px or `--text-2xs`/`--text-xs`. A venue theme that darkens paper without darkening subtle ink fails five pairs at once. `resolveVenueTheme()` should therefore derive `--text-subtle` *last*, from the already-resolved paper and sunken surfaces, rather than accepting it as an input.

**(d) The SC4 automated test — what it must assert.**
`tests/theme/venue-contrast-guardrail.test.ts`:
1. **Exhaustive sweep** over the finite curated palette × polarity × pairing set: for every input, `resolveVenueTheme(input).ok === true` and every `CONTRAST_PAIRS` row ≥ its threshold. This is deterministic and *complete* — the strongest possible proof, and it is only possible because D-03 made the set finite.
2. **Adversarial cases** that must be *rejected*: `#FFFFFF` brand on `#FFFFFF` paper, `#0b5fa5`-on-`#0b5fa5`, near-miss pairs at 4.49:1. A guardrail that has never refused anything is untested.
3. **Oracle pinning:** at least three literal known-good ratios (e.g. `#000`/`#fff` = 21, `#767676`/`#fff` ≈ 4.54, `#777`/`#fff` ≈ 4.48) so a refactor of the luminance maths fails here rather than silently loosening the gate.
4. **Non-vacuity control:** assert `CONTRAST_PAIRS.length ≥ 8` — the same idiom `theme-width-scale.test.ts` already uses ("if this ever becomes empty the shielding below is dead weight").
5. **D-10 lock:** assert no `prefers-color-scheme: dark` selector reaches any `--venue-*` token, since auto-darkening would invalidate every ratio measured above.

**Where it is enforced at runtime (Phase 4, contract authored here):** a `superRefine` on the venue-theme Zod schema in the Server Action write path — never client-only, since a direct PostgREST/RPC caller would bypass it. This mirrors the existing `createVenueSchema` philosophy verbatim ("Zod is the boundary that produces a usable error message before a round-trip; the CHECK constraints are the backstop that holds for any caller"). Consider a Postgres CHECK as the DB-level backstop in Phase 4.

### Pattern 4 — Migration ordering and the SC2 invariant (RQ6)

**How `app/globals.css` absorbs the token files.** CSS `@import` must precede every other rule except `@charset` and `@layer` statements. The existing file opens with three imports; the token imports join that block:

```css
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "tw-animate-css";
@import "shadcn/tailwind.css";
@import "./tokens/primitives.css";   /* spacing, shape, motion, type scale */
@import "./tokens/cena.css";         /* Cena product brand */
@import "./tokens/venue.css";        /* venue contract + fallbacks */
/* @custom-variant, @theme inline, :root, @layer base follow unchanged */
```

Tailwind v4's PostCSS plugin resolves these imports itself and processes `@theme` blocks inside imported files, so the split is purely organisational. `[ASSUMED — verified behaviour in Tailwind v4 generally; confirm on first build]`

**What in the 47-file / 462-test suite is coupled to appearance.** I grepped the whole suite for `className`, `toHaveClass`, `class=`, `data-slot`, and Tailwind class prefixes (`bg-`, `text-`, `border-`, `size-`, `max-w-`). **The complete result set is seven lines, all in one file:**

| File | Coupling | Risk under re-skin |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/lib/theme-width-scale.test.ts` | Parses `app/globals.css` for `--spacing-*`, `--max-width-*`, `--min-width-*`; oracles against `tailwindcss/theme.css` | **HIGH — the single hard constraint on the token layer.** It computes `collidingKeys` dynamically, so **any new `--spacing-<name>` that matches a Tailwind container name (`xs sm md lg xl 2xl 3xl 4xl…`) fails the suite until a matching `--max-width-*`/`--min-width-*` shield is added.** It also pins `--spacing-md: 16px` and `--spacing-touch: 44px` literally — the Cena spacing scale **must** preserve those two exact values or the test's meaning changes. |

**No test asserts on a Tailwind class string.** No test asserts on a colour. No snapshot tests exist. The re-skin's appearance surface is therefore essentially unguarded by the suite — which is good for SC2 and bad for SC3, and means SC3 needs its own evidence (see § Validation Architecture).

**What *is* coupled, in a way a careless re-skin breaks:** accessible names and roles, not classes.

| File | Depends on |
|---|---|
| `tests/venues/venue-form-languages.test.tsx` | `getByRole("checkbox", { name: "Română" \| "Magyar" \| "English" })`, `data-state` on the Radix checkbox, **`.disabled === true`**, `getByLabelText("Default language")` + `select.options` |
| `tests/lib/create-venue-affordance.test.tsx`, `tests/auth/google-affordance.test.tsx`, `tests/tablet/idle-relock.test.tsx` | rendered roles / accessible names |
| `tests/lib/unconditional-cta-coverage.test.ts` | **TypeScript AST** of `app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx` — asserts the `VENUE_CREATE_PATH` `<Link>` has **no conditional ancestor**, and that the constant is imported from `@/lib/venue-routes` |
| `tests/lib/venue-page-gate-coverage.test.ts`, `tests/auth/reset-stage-source.test.ts`, `tests/lib/device-cookie-outcome-coverage.test.ts`, `tests/lib/google-affordance-coverage.test.ts`, `tests/lib/server-action-exports.test.ts` | source text / AST of specific files |
| `tests/lib/route-error-boundary.test.ts` | file-tree shape under `app/(dashboard)/` |

**The re-skin rules that follow, directly:**
- Never remove or rename a `<Label htmlFor>` / `aria-label` while restyling.
- Keep Radix `data-state` semantics — a re-skin styles `data-checked`, it does not replace the state model.
- **Do not wrap the `(dashboard)/layout.tsx` create-venue `<Link>` in any conditional, ternary, or `&&`** — even for layout purposes. `unconditional-cta-coverage.test.ts` walks ancestors and will correctly go red.
- Do not convert `<select>` to a Radix `Select` in `venue-form.tsx` without also updating `venue-form-languages.test.tsx`'s `getByLabelText(...).options` reads — which would change an existing test's meaning and violate SC2. (Independently, SC3 argues for keeping native on mobile.)

**Safest ordering — tokens first, primitives second, surfaces third, defects last:**

| Wave | Work | Gate |
|---|---|---|
| **0** | D-12 archive (RQ10) — *before any repo change*; then the qr-menu verification (RQ1) | archive files exist on disk; 11 verdicts recorded |
| **1** | Token layer + fonts. `app/tokens/*`, `app/layout.tsx` fonts, `globals.css` imports. **No component touched.** | full suite green (this is where `theme-width-scale` bites); SC1 tripwire green; `pnpm build` clean |
| **2** | Add the 7 registry primitives. Nothing consumes them yet. | `pnpm exec tsc`; full suite green |
| **3** | Re-skin the 11 existing primitives, one commit each. | full suite green after **each** — a class-only change cannot break a behavioural test, so a red here is a real signal |
| **4** | Re-skin the surfaces (auth → dashboard → venue → staff → tablet). | full suite green; visual pass |
| **5** | **G-01-13 + G-01-14** and their new regression tests. Last, so the suite that proves them is already known-good against the new visual layer. | 462 existing green **+ 2 new**; `01-UAT.md` rows closed |
| **6** | Copy deck (D-04 lexicon + the six owed rows), design-project write-backs (D-11) | contract diff clean |

Rationale for defects last: putting them first means every later red is ambiguous between "the fix broke it" and "the re-skin broke it". Putting them last makes wave 5's diff the only suspect.

### Pattern 5 — G-01-13: the EUR venue that cannot be created (D-13)

**The mechanism, traced end-to-end and confirmed in source** `[VERIFIED: repo source + radix-ui@1.3.11 dist]`:

1. `CURRENCY_DEFAULTS.EUR = { countryCode: "", timezone: "", defaultLanguage: "en" }` (`lib/validation/venue.ts`).
2. `handleCurrencyChange("EUR")` sets `enabledLanguages = Array.from(new Set(["en", "en"]))` → **`["en"]`, length 1**.
3. `venue-form.tsx` renders `disabled={enabledLanguages.length === 1 && enabledLanguages[0] === code}` — so the English checkbox is `disabled`.
4. `CheckboxPrimitive.Root` forwards `disabled` to `CheckboxBubbleInput`, which renders `<Primitive.input type="checkbox" aria-hidden name={name} value={value} disabled={disabled} …>` — verified at `@radix-ui/react-checkbox@1.3.11/dist/index.mjs:250-262`. **That bubble input is the only thing that puts `enabledLanguages` into `FormData`.**
5. HTML omits disabled controls from form submission, so `formData.getAll("enabledLanguages")` returns `[]`.
6. `createVenueSchema.enabledLanguages.min(1)` rejects → "Enable at least one language." — pointing at a checkbox the owner cannot tick.

RON and HUF are unaffected because both seed **two** languages, so nothing is ever disabled.

**The idiomatic fix, and why the obvious one is wrong.**

❌ **Re-enable the checkbox and guard server-side.** This changes the meaning of an existing test — `venue-form-languages.test.tsx` asserts `checkboxFor("ro").disabled === true` under an explicit WR-08 rationale ("the refusal is visible rather than a dead click"). SC2 forbids it, and the UX rationale is sound.

❌ **`readOnly` on the Radix checkbox.** Radix `Checkbox.Root` has no `readOnly` prop; `aria-readonly` would not restore the value.

✅ **Keep `disabled`, add a sibling hidden input for exactly the disabled-and-checked case.** Minimal, preserves the visible refusal, preserves the test, restores the FormData value:

```tsx
<Checkbox
  id={`language-${code}`}
  name="enabledLanguages"
  value={code}
  checked={enabledLanguages.includes(code)}
  disabled={isLastEnabled(code)}
  onCheckedChange={(checked) => toggleLanguage(code, checked === true)}
/>
{/*
 * G-01-13. The checkbox above is `disabled` so the refusal is VISIBLE (WR-08),
 * and Radix forwards `disabled` to the hidden bubble input it uses to carry the
 * value — which HTML then omits from FormData. For an EUR venue the enabled set
 * seeds to exactly ["en"], so the only enabled language was the disabled one and
 * `enabledLanguages` arrived empty. This restores the value without re-enabling
 * the control, so the refusal stays visible and the form stays submittable.
 */}
{isLastEnabled(code) ? (
  <input type="hidden" name="enabledLanguages" value={code} />
) : null}
```

The `isLastEnabled(code)` guard is what prevents a duplicate value when the control is enabled. `enabledLanguages` is a `z.array(...).min(1)`, so even a duplicate would parse — but the RPC would receive `["en","en"]`, so the guard is load-bearing, not cosmetic.

**What the new regression test must assert** (`tests/venues/venue-eur-submission.test.tsx`, jsdom):
1. Switch currency to EUR; assert exactly one language checkbox remains checked **and** that it is `disabled` (proves the WR-08 refusal survived the fix).
2. Read the enclosing `<form>`'s `new FormData(form)` and assert `getAll("enabledLanguages")` **equals `["en"]`** — not just non-empty, and **exactly one entry**, which is the assertion that catches the duplicate-value regression.
3. Control: with currency `RON` (two languages, nothing disabled), assert `getAll("enabledLanguages")` equals `["ro","en"]` — proving the hidden input did not fire when it should not.
4. Assert `createVenueSchema.safeParse(...)` on the harvested FormData succeeds — closing the loop on the actual failure mode rather than on a proxy for it.

Assertion (2) is the one that fails today. Assertion (3) is the one that fails if the fix is naive.

### Pattern 6 — G-01-14: the stale venue switcher (D-13)

**The mechanism.** `actions/venues.ts` ends with `redirect(`/venues/${venueId}`)` and calls no cache API. `VenueSwitcher` is rendered by `app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx`, which is **shared** between `/venues/new` and `/venues/[venueId]`. On a soft navigation Next reuses the cached shared-layout segment rather than re-rendering it, so the switcher shows the pre-creation venue list. For a first-to-second-venue owner this is worse than a stale name: `VenueSwitcher` returns `null` below two venues, so the switcher **fails to appear at all** on the exact transition that creates the need for it.

**The correct call, and where.** `revalidatePath('/', 'layout')` immediately before `redirect(...)`.

- **Placement is load-bearing:** `redirect()` signals by throwing, so anything after it never runs. Next's own docs state it plainly: *"If `redirect` is called, any code after it does not run, so revalidation calls should be placed before `redirect` if the destination needs fresh data."* `[CITED: nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/server-actions]`
- **Why `'/'` + `'layout'` and not `/venues`:** the `(dashboard)` route group is invisible in the URL, so there is no path that *is* the dashboard layout. Next's docs: *"If `path` is `/` and `type` is `'layout'`, it purges the Client Cache and invalidates all cached data."* `[CITED: nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath]` Purging the client Router Cache is exactly and only what this defect needs — the layout is already dynamic (`cookies()`), so no server-side cache entry is being wastefully discarded.
- **`revalidatePath('/venues', 'layout')` is the tighter alternative** and is defensible; it invalidates `/venues` and everything beneath it sharing that layout. Prefer it if the planner wants minimal blast radius. It is *not* obviously sufficient for a future sibling route outside `/venues` that also renders the switcher, which is why `'/'` is the recommendation.
- Next forwards pending revalidations to the redirect target via `NEXT_CACHE_REVALIDATED_TAGS_HEADER`, so the fresh switcher arrives in the **same** round trip — no extra request, no flash of the stale list. `[CITED: next/src/server/app-render/action-handler.ts]`
- **Do not reach for `updateTag`.** Next 16 offers it for Cache Components read-your-own-writes, but this repo has no `cacheTag` on the venue read and CLAUDE.md prescribes `revalidatePath`. Introducing a tagging scheme here is scope the phase does not need.

**Concretely:**

```ts
import { revalidatePath } from "next/cache";
// …
  if (error || !venueId) {
    return { status: "error", formError: COPY.errors.venueCreation, values };
  }

  /*
   * G-01-14. The (dashboard) layout renders VenueSwitcher and is SHARED between
   * /venues/new and /venues/[venueId], so a soft navigation reuses the cached
   * layout segment and the switcher lists the pre-creation set. For an owner
   * creating their SECOND venue that is not a stale label — VenueSwitcher
   * returns null below two venues, so the control does not appear at all on the
   * one transition that creates the need for it.
   *
   * '/' + 'layout' purges the client Router Cache, which is the only cache in
   * play (this layout is already dynamic via cookies()). It must precede
   * redirect(), which signals by throwing.
   */
  revalidatePath("/", "layout");

  redirect(`/venues/${venueId}`);
```

**What the new regression test must assert** (`tests/actions/create-venue-revalidation.test.ts`, node env). This is a *sequencing* assertion, not a rendering one:
1. `vi.mock("next/cache")` and `vi.mock("next/navigation")`; make the `redirect` mock **throw**, as the real one does.
2. Assert `revalidatePath` was called **exactly once**, with `("/", "layout")` — pin both arguments, since `revalidatePath("/")` without the type is a no-op for this defect and would otherwise pass.
3. Assert **ordering**: `revalidatePath.mock.invocationCallOrder[0] < redirect.mock.invocationCallOrder[0]`. Without this the test passes against a version that revalidates after the throw — i.e. never.
4. Assert `revalidatePath` is **not** called on the failure paths (`!user`, `!account`, RPC error) — those return a `CreateVenueState` and must not purge the client cache.

Assertion (3) is the one that distinguishes a real fix from a cosmetic one.

**`01-UAT.md` bookkeeping both fixes owe:** flip `G-01-13` and `G-01-14` from `parked` to `resolved` with `resolved_by`/`resolved_at`; update `## Parked Gaps` to leave only `G-01-16`; tick **ACCT-03**; note that **test 26**, the outcome roll-up, becomes unblocked on the G-01-13 leg (`ACCT-01` still needs the Google browser leg, so the roll-up does not fully close).
