The audit's "16 primitives, 11 exist, 10 missing" does not add up and is wrong in both directions. Verified against `https://ui.shadcn.com/r/styles/radix-nova/<name>.json` and the repo's `components/ui/`:

| DS primitive | In repo today | Available at `radix-nova`? | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Button | `button.tsx` | yes | **re-skin** |
| **IconButton** | `button.tsx` `size="icon"\|"icon-xs"\|"icon-sm"\|"icon-lg"` | n/a | **NOT net-new** — a Button size, already shipped |
| **Icon** | none (lucide used directly) | **no registry item** | **hand-author** — a ~15-line wrapper pinning `strokeWidth={1.75}`. Arguably a lint rule instead |
| Card | `card.tsx` | yes | **re-skin** |
| Badge | `badge.tsx` | yes | **re-skin** |
| **Tag** | none | **no registry item** | **hand-author or a Badge variant.** No Radix behaviour involved. Note `Badge` already ships 6 variants — a 7th may suffice |
| Input | `input.tsx` | yes | **re-skin** |
| **Select** | none (raw `<select>` in `venue-form.tsx`) | **yes** (`select`, and `native-select`) | **`add` + re-skin.** But see the SC3 caveat below |
| Checkbox | `checkbox.tsx` | yes | **re-skin** |
| **Radio** | none | **yes** (`radio-group`) | **`add` + re-skin** |
| **Switch** | none | **yes** (`switch`) | **`add` + re-skin** |
| **Field** | none (`components/field-error.tsx` overlaps) | **yes** (`field` → pulls `label` + `separator`) | **`add` + re-skin.** Reconcile with `field-error.tsx` |
| **Tabs** | none | **yes** (`tabs`) | **`add` + re-skin** |
| Dialog | `dialog.tsx` | yes | **re-skin** |
| **Toast** | **`sonner.tsx` (already wired)** | **NO — `radix-nova/toast.json` returns 404** | **ALREADY COVERED.** Keep sonner |
| **Tooltip** | none | **yes** (`tooltip`) | **`add` + re-skin** |

**Accurate net-new count: 6 CLI adds + 1 transitive (`separator`) = 7 new files. 0–2 hand-authored. 2 of the audit's "10 missing" were never missing.**

**And the audit's 16 is not a superset of the re-skin surface.** The repo also ships **`alert.tsx`, `avatar.tsx`, `dropdown-menu.tsx`** — all three used by shipped Phase 01 surfaces, none named by the DS. Leaving them un-re-skinned produces a visibly mixed system. SC2's "all 16 primitives" therefore **understates the work by three**; the plan should say so rather than silently over- or under-delivering.

**`shadcn add` mechanics for this repo, verified:**
- The CLI reads `style` from `components.json` (`radix-nova`); `--style` was dropped and `new-york` no longer exists.
- All six items declare `cssVars: false`, `css: false`, `tailwind: false` — **none will mutate `app/globals.css`.** Verified per-item.
- All six import from `radix-ui` (the single package already installed) — no new npm dependency.
- The raw registry JSON contains `IconPlaceholder` imports from `@/app/(create)/components/icon-placeholder`. **That is a registry-authoring artifact; the CLI substitutes the configured `iconLibrary` (`lucide`) on install.** The repo's existing `checkbox.tsx` — which imports `CheckIcon` from `lucide-react` — is the proof this transform runs. Do not "fix" the placeholder by hand.
- **`field` lists `label` as a registry dependency and `components/ui/label.tsx` already exists.** Run with an explicit overwrite policy; an unattended overwrite silently reverts `label.tsx`, and `.design-sync/NOTES.md` documents a real quirk in it (`peer-disabled:` can never fire in this system's field pattern — the working mechanism is a `group` wrapper with `data-disabled`).
- `shadcn add form` adds nothing here — forms use `useActionState` + Zod. Do not put it in a plan.

**SC3 caveat on `Select`.** `radix-nova/select` is a styled listbox. On a phone, the native `<select>` currently in `venue-form.tsx` opens the OS picker, which is strictly better one-handed — and `native-select` exists in the registry for precisely that. Swapping to the Radix `Select` would also break `venue-form-languages.test.tsx`'s `select.options` reads, violating SC2. **Recommendation: keep native `<select>` on the venue form; adopt `Select` only where a listbox is genuinely required.**

**Touch targets — a live SC3 risk.** The `radix-nova` `Button` ships `h-6 / h-7 / h-8 / h-9` (24–36px) and `size-6 / size-7 / size-8 / size-9` for icon buttons. **Every one is below the DS's 44px minimum and below the 44px floor `--spacing-touch` already encodes.** `01-UI-SPEC.md` applies the 44px floor only to the tablet route group; SC3 extends "usable one-handed on a phone" to *every* owner surface. The re-skin must add a phone-appropriate size (or raise the defaults) — this is real design work, not a token swap, and the planner should scope it explicitly.

### Pattern 9 — Language detection and switching on a prerendered page (LANG-05, LANG-06)

**The problem, precisely.** The template detects language by reading `navigator.languages` on first paint. CLAUDE.md mandates a statically-generated, CDN-edge-served diner page with zero DB round-trip and explicitly rejects client-rendered data fetching. Those are incompatible: a client-side language read means either a full-menu flash of the wrong language after hydration, or a client-rendered page.

**The mechanism, ranked.**

1. **One static page per (venue, language) + `Accept-Language` redirect at the edge — recommended.**
   - Route: `/menu/[slug]/[lang]`, `generateStaticParams()` over `venue.enabledLanguages`. Every rendered page is fully static, fully prerendered, and fully cacheable — the diner's language costs zero dynamic rendering.
   - `/menu/[slug]` (no language) redirects in **`proxy.ts`** — Next 16's renamed middleware — running the template's own matching policy against the `Accept-Language` header instead of `navigator.languages`. `proxy.ts` executes *before* the cache, so a redirect there does not de-optimise the destination.
   - **LANG-06 falls out for free:** the language pills become `<Link>`s to a sibling static URL. "For the rest of the visit" is then carried by the URL — surviving reload, back/forward and sharing — with zero storage, zero cookie, and therefore zero interaction with CLAUDE.md's "no consent banner, ever" stance. (A language cookie *would* be consent-exempt as strictly-necessary under ePrivacy Art. 5(3), but not needing the argument is better than winning it.)
   - **Cost:** one 307 on the un-languaged entry, i.e. one extra RTT on a poor connection — the exact thing DINE-03 guards. **Mitigation worth planning:** encode the venue's default language directly in the QR payload (`/menu/[slug]/[defaultLang]`), so the common case never redirects at all and only a diner whose `Accept-Language` disagrees pays the hop. This costs nothing and is decided at QR-generation time (DINE-01, Phase 2).
2. Prerender all languages into one document and toggle client-side — multiplies the payload on a bandwidth-constrained surface. **Reject.**
3. Read `Accept-Language` in the page component — forces the route dynamic. **Reject.**
4. Client-side `navigator` read (what the template does) — flash or client-render. **Reject.**

**What ports verbatim from the template.** The matching policy itself, which is well judged: iterate the client's ordered preference list, normalise each tag to its lowercased 2-char prefix, return the first that is in the supported set, else `'en'`. Ordered-preference matching (rather than first-tag-only) is the part usually got wrong. Run it against parsed `Accept-Language` q-values instead of `navigator.languages`.

**Also port:** the `t.detected` disclosure line — *"Set from your phone's language. Change it whenever you like."* — in all three languages. It turns an automatic decision into an explained one, and it should become a Copywriting Contract row.

**Fix on the way through:** use endonyms on the pills (Magyar / English / Română), not two-letter codes — a diner who cannot read the current language cannot necessarily decode "HU". Add `role="group"` with an accessible label and `aria-current="true"` on the active pill; the template has neither.

### Pattern 10 — Currency formatting (ACCT-02, W-3)

**Use `Intl.NumberFormat`. Do not port the template's `money()`.**

The template's formatter hardcodes FX rates, bakes a rounding decision into display, and omits thousands grouping for RON and EUR. What it gets *right* — and what settles audit warning W-3 — is that **formatting is per-currency, not one continental rule**: HUF is zero-decimal with space grouping and a trailing `Ft`; RON and EUR use a comma decimal separator with a trailing symbol. The design project's `readme.md` still mandates the wrong global rule and should be corrected in the same write-back as D-11/D-04.

Verified on this machine (Node 24.14.1, ICU 78.2) `[VERIFIED: local execution]`:

```ts
// lib/format/money.ts
const LOCALE: Record<Currency, string> = { HUF: "hu-HU", RON: "ro-RO", EUR: "de-DE" };

export function formatPrice(minor: number, currency: Currency, locale = LOCALE[currency]) {
  return new Intl.NumberFormat(locale, {
    style: "currency",
    currency,
    // REQUIRED for RON: the default `symbol` display renders "RON", not "lei".
    currencyDisplay: "narrowSymbol",
  }).format(minor);
}
```

| Input | Output | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `148500 HUF` | `"148 500 Ft"` | ✓ zero decimals, space grouping |
| `7900 HUF` | `"7900 Ft"` | ⚠ **no grouping at 4 digits** — ICU's `minimumGroupingDigits` for `hu-HU`. The template emits `"7 900 Ft"`. A real, visible divergence: decide deliberately |
| `1903.85 RON` | `"1.903,85 lei"` | ✓ correct `.` grouping the template lacks — **and `narrowSymbol` is what makes it "lei" rather than "RON"** |
| `20.26 EUR` | `"20,26 €"` | ✓ |

**Two things to pin with a unit test asserting literal strings**, because ICU data shifts between Node majors: the `narrowSymbol` → `lei` mapping, and the 4-digit HUF grouping behaviour. Both are cheap to assert and expensive to discover in production.

**Do not port:** FX conversion (venues store one currency — `venues.currency` already exists and is CHECK-constrained), and HUF's `Math.round(huf/10)*10`, which is a pricing decision masquerading as formatting.

### Pattern 11 — Writing back to the design project (D-11, D-04, W-3)

**`DesignSync` can write** — `finalize_plan` → `write_files` `[VERIFIED: coordinator, this session]`. So D-11 is an **automatable task, not a manual checkpoint** — which resolves the concern this research originally raised. Two constraints shape how the task must be written:

1. **It is a write to the design project, not a repo edit.** It produces no repo diff, so it cannot be verified by the usual gates and must not be bundled into a plan whose verification is "tests green". Give it its own task with its own evidence (a re-read of the written file).
2. **It needs its own `finalize_plan` approval**, which is a distinct gate from GSD's. Plan for it as an approval step, not as a silent side effect.

**Three edits land in the same file (`readme.md`) and should be one task, not three:**

| # | Decision | Current wording | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **D-11** | Paragraph 1: *"One system covers the floor (tables, tickets, payment), the book (reservations, waitlist, guests) and the back office (menu, staff, nightly numbers), so a small dining room does not need four vendors and a clipboard."* | Rewrite around tiered entry landing on the QR menu. This is verbatim the all-or-nothing suite PROJECT.md names as the competitor gap Cena exists to attack |
| 2 | **D-04** | § Content fundamentals: *"**Restaurant words, not software words.** Covers, turns, the pass, fired, 86'd, the book, walk-in, close out."* + four worked examples using them | Re-cut to menu-tier vocabulary; replace the examples. **Keep the register verbatim** |
| 3 | **W-3** | *"Continental decimal comma for currency; €148,50"* as a global rule | Replace with the per-currency convention (Pattern 10). The qr-menu template already contradicts this rule correctly |

**Why this compounds:** `readme.md` is the brief every future `/gsd-ui-phase` reads. Leaving it wrong mis-briefs every later design pass — which, per the audit, is exactly how blocker B-1 entered the system in the first place. **The kits are left untouched** (D-11).

**Author the replacement text in the repo first** — e.g. `.planning/design-archive/readme-corrections.md` — so the write-back task is "apply this text", reviewable in a normal diff, rather than "compose and write" inside an unreviewable step.

## Don't Hand-Roll

| Problem | Don't Build | Use Instead | Why |
|---------|-------------|-------------|-----|
| Self-hosting + subsetting webfonts | A `pyftsubset` build step or committed `.woff2` blobs | `next/font/google` with `subsets: ["latin","latin-ext"]` | Handles unicode-range splitting, `size-adjust` fallback metrics (CLS), preload tags, and build caching. Also sidesteps IBM Plex Mono's Reserved Font Name. `pyftsubset` is not installed here and fontTools is absent |
| Focus management, keyboard nav, ARIA on Select/Radio/Switch/Tabs/Tooltip | The DS's hand-rolled JSX primitives | `radix-nova` registry items on `radix-ui` | Audit D-2 already decided this; the DS primitives carry no focus trap, no roving tabindex, no `aria-*` |
| Toast stacking, queueing, dismissal, reduced-motion | Anything | `sonner` (already wired, UI-SPEC E11) | No `radix-nova` toast exists to replace it |
| Icon set | Importing a second icon library | `lucide-react` at `strokeWidth={1.75}` | Already a dependency; DS's 50 glyphs *are* Lucide |
| Per-venue theme delivery | A client fetch, a cookie read, or middleware | Values baked into the prerendered HTML via a `style` prop | CLAUDE.md forbids a DB round-trip and a client fetch on the diner path |
| oklch → sRGB conversion (**if** venue tokens end up in oklch) | A hand-rolled colour-space conversion | `culori` (devDep) — **or, better, constrain the venue contract to hex** | Colour-space maths is where a "close enough" implementation quietly under-reports a contrast ratio on a legal gate |
| **Currency formatting** | The template's `money()` — hand-rolled regex grouping, `.replace('.',',')`, hardcoded FX | `Intl.NumberFormat` with `currencyDisplay: "narrowSymbol"` | Grouping rules, decimal counts and symbol placement differ per locale and change over time. The template's version has no RON/EUR grouping and bakes a rounding decision into display. See Pattern 10 |
| **`Accept-Language` negotiation** | A hand-rolled q-value parser | A small well-scoped parser **or** `@formatjs/intl-localematcher` | Only if the ordered-preference matching in Pattern 9 grows beyond the template's 6-line policy. The 6-line version is fine for a 3-language supported set — do not add a dependency prematurely |
| **The item-detail bottom sheet** | Porting the template's `div` + backdrop-click | Radix `Dialog` (already at `components/ui/dialog.tsx`) | The template's sheet has no `role="dialog"`, no `aria-modal`, no focus trap, no Escape handler and no focus restore. Take the visuals only |
| **Exception — WCAG 2.1 relative luminance** | *(this one you SHOULD hand-roll)* | ~15 lines in `lib/theme/contrast.ts` | The formula is normative and frozen. A dependency inside a legal release gate is supply-chain surface for zero benefit — and `wcag-contrast`'s last publish was 2019 |

**Key insight:** in this phase the "don't hand-roll" line is drawn at *behaviour and browser quirks* (font loading, focus management, colour-space conversion), not at *frozen arithmetic*. The contrast ratio is the one place a dependency buys nothing and costs a supply-chain surface on a gate that is legally load-bearing.

## Common Pitfalls

### Pitfall 1 — A new `--spacing-<name>` silently collapses every page shell
**What goes wrong:** Adding a Cena spacing token whose name collides with a Tailwind container name (`xs sm md lg xl 2xl 3xl`) makes `max-w-<name>` resolve to the spacing value. `max-w-md` became `16px`, and because `Card` is `overflow-hidden`, the login form was clipped out of both paint *and* hit-testing — present, enabled, invisible, unclickable.
**Why it happens:** Tailwind v4 resolves `max-w-*` as `--max-width → --spacing → --container`; `--spacing` outranks `--container`.
**How to avoid:** For every `--spacing-<k>` added, add matching `--max-width-<k>` and `--min-width-<k>` with Tailwind's container value. `tests/lib/theme-width-scale.test.ts` enforces this dynamically and will name the missing key.
**Warning signs:** `theme-width-scale.test.ts` red; any page shell rendering as a narrow sliver.

### Pitfall 2 — `@theme` without `inline` makes the venue theme un-overridable
**What goes wrong:** Venue colour changes have no visible effect, or affect the whole document instead of the menu subtree.
**Why it happens:** Non-inline `@theme` emits `--color-x: var(--venue-ink)` in `:root`, resolving `--venue-ink` in `:root`'s scope; a nested override is ignored.
**How to avoid:** Every venue-themable token goes in `@theme inline`.
**Warning signs:** The token's value in devtools resolves to the fallback despite the wrapper element carrying the override.

### Pitfall 3 — Fixing G-01-13 by re-enabling the checkbox
**What goes wrong:** `venue-form-languages.test.tsx` goes red on `expect(checkboxFor("ro").disabled).toBe(true)`, and the WR-08 "visible refusal" UX is lost.
**How to avoid:** Keep `disabled`; add a sibling hidden input, guarded so it fires only for the disabled-and-checked case.
**Warning signs:** A diff that touches the `disabled=` expression in `venue-form.tsx`.

### Pitfall 4 — `revalidatePath` after `redirect`
**What goes wrong:** The fix appears in the diff, ships, and does nothing. `redirect()` throws; nothing after it runs.
**How to avoid:** Call it before `redirect`, and make the regression test assert `invocationCallOrder`.
**Warning signs:** A test that only asserts `revalidatePath` "was called".

### Pitfall 5 — `shadcn add field` silently reverts `label.tsx`
**What goes wrong:** `field` lists `label` as a registry dependency; an unattended overwrite reverts the existing file and discards the documented `peer-disabled` workaround.
**How to avoid:** Add `field` with an explicit overwrite policy and diff `components/ui/label.tsx` afterwards.
**Warning signs:** `label.tsx` appearing in a diff for a plan that never mentioned it.

### Pitfall 6 — SC1's literal wording is already false, and the check will encode a lie
**What goes wrong:** A "no third-party asset" test is written, immediately fails on `https://accounts.google.com/gsi/client` (`app/(auth)/components/GoogleOneTap.tsx:422`), and gets narrowed until it can no longer fail.
**Why it happens:** SC1 says "no third-party font **or asset** request on any page", but Google sign-in is ACCT-01 — a shipped feature, not an oversight.
**How to avoid:** Write the check as an **allowlist with exactly one entry**, carrying its ACCT-01 justification inline. Any new external origin fails until it is added with a reason. This is the same idiom `unconditional-cta-coverage.test.ts` uses.
**Warning signs:** A check scoped so narrowly it only ever looks at `globals.css`.

### Pitfall 7 — The re-skin pushes a Server Component to the client
**What goes wrong:** Adding a `Tooltip` or a hover-state hook to `DashboardNav` / `VenueSwitcher` / `(dashboard)/layout.tsx` requires `"use client"`, which moves the venue read to the client, breaks RSC-payload nav delivery, and puts a Supabase call on the browser.
**How to avoid:** Keep interactive leaves in their own client components. `VenueSwitcher` (server, does the read) → `venue-switcher-menu.tsx` (client) is the pattern already in the repo — follow it.
**Warning signs:** `"use client"` appearing at the top of any file under `app/(dashboard)/` that performs a Supabase query.

### Pitfall 8 — Changing the app font silently breaks the design-sync preview bundle
**What goes wrong:** Previews render in browser-default serif and the contact sheets photograph the wrong thing, with nothing failing.
**Why it happens:** `.design-sync/fonts/` holds Inter files harvested from `.next/static/media`, and `.design-sync/tailwind-entry.css` *defines* `--font-sans` for the out-of-Next context. Neither follows a font change. `.design-sync/NOTES.md` states this explicitly.
**How to avoid:** Treat `.design-sync/fonts/*`, `.design-sync/tailwind-entry.css` and its `@source inline(...)` token safelist as part of the token migration's blast radius. Note the safelist enumerates the token vocabulary — **new tokens will not appear in the bundle CSS until added there.**

### Pitfall 9 — The 44px touch floor is treated as tablet-only
**What goes wrong:** Owner surfaces re-skin onto `h-8` (32px) buttons and SC3's "usable one-handed on a phone" fails at review, after every surface is done.
**How to avoid:** Decide the phone-surface control height in Wave 1 (token layer), not Wave 4 (surfaces).

### Pitfall 10 — "Adopt `tokens/*.css`" silently reintroduces the Google Fonts CDN
**What goes wrong:** SC1 is delivered, then regressed in the same wave, because `tokens/fonts.css` is one of the `tokens/*.css` files and it is a bare `@import url('https://fonts.googleapis.com/…')`.
**How to avoid:** name the exclusion explicitly in the plan text, not just in the researcher's head. The SC1 tripwire catches it — but only if it is written before the token layer lands, which is why both are Wave 1.
**Warning signs:** any task whose action reads "copy `tokens/` across" without an exclusion list.

### Pitfall 11 — Carrying the template's 7-allergen vocabulary forward
**What goes wrong:** Phase 3 implements DINE-06 against the template's `AL` map, and Cena ships a product in which a restaurant physically cannot declare peanuts, sesame, mustard, soy, crustaceans, molluscs or lupin.
**Why it happens:** the template README says "Allergens are the EU set." It is 7 of 14.
**How to avoid:** treat the vocabulary as net-new work in Phase 3, sourced from Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011 Annex II, with **peanuts distinct from tree nuts**. Consider a unit test asserting `ALLERGENS.length === 14` with the Annex II reference in the failure message.
**Warning signs:** an allergen enum with 7 entries; a `nuts` key with no `peanuts` sibling.

### Pitfall 12 — Porting the template's language detection
**What goes wrong:** `navigator.languages` is read on the client, and either the whole menu flashes from English to Hungarian after hydration on a 3G connection, or the page silently becomes client-rendered and the CDN/ISR strategy is lost.
**How to avoid:** Pattern 9 — one static page per (venue, language), `Accept-Language` negotiated as a redirect in `proxy.ts`.
**Warning signs:** `navigator` or `"use client"` anywhere near the menu route; a single `/menu/[slug]` route with a language state.

### Pitfall 13 — Copying `now: true` and `updatedLine`
**What goes wrong:** the "Now" badge is permanently on the dinner menu (it is a hardcoded literal, not a clock read), and the footer shows `4 · 8 · 19:04` forever.
**How to avoid:** both are demo data. Derive `now` server-side at prerender from the venue's timezone; derive the updated line from a real `generatedAt`. DINE-04's D-07 banner depends on the second one existing.

### Pitfall 14 — Two flaky tests get misread as re-skin regressions
**What goes wrong:** `tests/staff/pin-verify-backoff.test.ts` and `tests/actions/venue-authority.test.ts` are timing-flaky against local Postgres. A red there mid-migration sends someone hunting a phantom.
**How to avoid:** Re-run before treating either as real. Failures **anywhere else** are genuine — the suite has no other known flake.

## Code Examples

### Declaring the Cena pairing (SC1, D-09)

```tsx
// app/layout.tsx
// Newsreader and Instrument Sans are VARIABLE (opsz+wght / wdth+wght), so `weight`
// is optional. IBM Plex Mono is NOT variable — `weight` is REQUIRED or the build errors.
// subsets: latin + latin-ext is verified to cover every RO (ă â î ș ț) and HU (ő ű)
// diacritic for all three families, against fonts.google.com/metadata/fonts.
import { Newsreader, Instrument_Sans, IBM_Plex_Mono } from "next/font/google";

const serif = Newsreader({
  variable: "--font-serif",
  subsets: ["latin", "latin-ext"],
  display: "swap",
});

const sans = Instrument_Sans({
  variable: "--font-sans",
  subsets: ["latin", "latin-ext"],
  display: "swap",
});

const mono = IBM_Plex_Mono({
  variable: "--font-mono",
  subsets: ["latin", "latin-ext"],
  weight: ["400", "600"],   // non-variable: enumerate exactly what is used
  display: "swap",
  preload: false,           // only if mono is NOT on the diner critical path
});
```

### The venue token contract (Pattern 2)

```css
/* app/tokens/venue.css — fallbacks only. NO Cena hue may appear in this file (D-02). */
@theme inline {
  /* `inline` is REQUIRED: it makes utilities emit var(--venue-*) so a nested
     override on the menu root actually wins. Without it Tailwind resolves the
     reference in :root's scope and the override is ignored. */
  --color-venue-paper:      var(--venue-paper,      #ffffff);
  --color-venue-surface:    var(--venue-surface,    #f7f7f5);
  --color-venue-ink:        var(--venue-ink,        #1a1a1a);
  --color-venue-muted-ink:  var(--venue-muted-ink,  #5a5a5a);
  --color-venue-accent:     var(--venue-accent,     #1a1a1a);
  --color-venue-accent-ink: var(--venue-accent-ink, #ffffff);
  --color-venue-rule:       var(--venue-rule,       #e4e4e0);

  --font-venue-display: var(--font-venue-display, var(--font-serif));
  --font-venue-body:    var(--font-venue-body,    var(--font-sans));
}
```

```tsx
// app/menu/[slug]/page.tsx  — Phase 2 consumes this; 01.1 only authors the contract.
// Values are read at PRERENDER time and baked into static HTML: zero DB round-trip
// on the diner's request path, zero extra network request, no FOUC, no client fetch.
export default async function MenuPage({ params }: { params: Promise<{ slug: string }> }) {
  const { slug } = await params;
  const venue = await getVenueForPrerender(slug);
  const theme = resolveVenueTheme(venue.themeInput);
  if (!theme.ok) throw new Error("venue theme failed the AA guardrail");

  return (
    <div
      // A style prop, not a <style> tag: React escapes the value and there is no
      // string-interpolation injection surface. The pairing class is one of a
      // CLOSED set, because next/font resolves family names at build time.
      className={`${PAIRINGS[venue.pairingId].className} min-h-dvh bg-venue-paper text-venue-ink`}
      style={theme.tokens as React.CSSProperties}
    >
      {/* Cena structure. Venue skin. No --szeged-* anywhere below this line. */}
    </div>
  );
}
```

### The contrast guardrail (SC4)

```ts
// lib/theme/contrast.ts — WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.3. Pure, dependency-free, frozen maths.
function channel(c: number): number {
  const s = c / 255;
  return s <= 0.04045 ? s / 12.92 : ((s + 0.055) / 1.055) ** 2.4;
}

function relativeLuminance(hex: string): number {
  const n = parseInt(hex.replace("#", ""), 16);
  return (
    0.2126 * channel((n >> 16) & 255) +
    0.7152 * channel((n >> 8) & 255) +
    0.0722 * (n & 255)
  );
}

/** WCAG 2.1 contrast ratio, 1..21. Both arguments must be #rrggbb sRGB. */
export function contrastRatio(fg: string, bg: string): number {
  const a = relativeLuminance(fg);
  const b = relativeLuminance(bg);
  const [hi, lo] = a > b ? [a, b] : [b, a];
  return (hi + 0.05) / (lo + 0.05);
}

// APCA is perceptually better but is NOT WCAG 2.x, and SC4 names "WCAG AA 4.5:1"
// explicitly. Swapping algorithms would make the success criterion unfalsifiable.
export const AA_TEXT = 4.5;      // WCAG 1.4.3 — normal text
export const AA_NON_TEXT = 3.0;  // WCAG 1.4.11 — UI components / graphical objects
```

## Runtime State Inventory

01.1 is a migration phase, so the question is: *after every file in the repo is updated, what still carries the old visual layer?*

| Category | Items Found | Action Required |
|----------|-------------|------------------|
| **Stored data** | **None.** No design token, colour, font or theme value is persisted anywhere. `supabase/migrations/*` define no theme column; venue theming lands in Phase 4. Verified by grep across `supabase/` and `lib/`. | none |
| **Live service config** | **The claude.ai/design project `07b799d4-…` itself.** Four items live only there: (1) the D-12 archive — **confirmed against the live manifest 2026-08-04, all ten paths exist**: `ui_kits/service/{FloorPlan,PaymentView,ServiceApp,ServiceChrome,TicketView}.jsx` + `README.md` + `index.html` (7), `ui_kits/back-office/TheBook.jsx`, `guidelines/color-service-states.card.html`; (2) the D-11 positioning statement in `readme.md`; (3) the D-04 lexicon rule + four worked examples in `readme.md`; (4) the W-3 global currency rule in `readme.md`. **`.planning/design-archive/` does not exist.** | **Wave 0, before any repo change:** pull the 9 archive paths (10 files) into `.planning/design-archive/`. **Wave 6:** one write-back task covering all three `readme.md` edits — `DesignSync` **can write** (`finalize_plan` → `write_files`), so this is a task, not a checkpoint, but it needs its own `finalize_plan` approval. See Pattern 11 |
| **Design-project mirror (new)** | `.planning/research/design-system-mirror/` — 3 files pulled 2026-08-04. It is a **snapshot, not a sync**, and the live project has already moved once mid-phase | Re-fetch before implementing against any detail. Do **not** let the mirror become a competing source of truth for `readme.md` — that is why only excerpts were mirrored |
| **OS-registered state** | **None.** No scheduled task, launchd plist, pm2 process or systemd unit references the design system. | none |
| **Secrets / env vars** | **None.** `.env.example` and `.env.local` contain no font, design-system or theme key. No API key is needed for `next/font/google` (it fetches unauthenticated at build). | none |
| **Build artifacts / installed packages** | **Five, all stale after this phase:** (1) `.next/static/media/*.woff2` — 7 Inter files, regenerated on build; (2) **`.design-sync/fonts/inter-latin*.woff2` + `inter.css` — COMMITTED harvested copies that `NOTES.md` says will NOT follow a font change**; (3) `.design-sync/tailwind-entry.css` — defines `--font-sans` for the preview context and safelists the token vocabulary via `@source inline(...)`; **new tokens are invisible to the bundle until added here**; (4) `.design-sync/.cache/cena.css` — a compiled snapshot of `globals.css`, regenerated only by `build.sh`; (5) `ds-bundle/` — compiled bundle plus 15 `_screenshots/*.png` photographing the **old** visual layer | Re-run `.design-sync/build.sh` after the token layer lands. Re-harvest or replace `.design-sync/fonts/`. Extend the `@source inline(...)` safelist. Treat `ds-bundle/_screenshots/*` as expected-to-change, not as regressions |
| **Design-sync config** | `.design-sync/config.json` targets **deleted** project `25b3418f-b297-4143-8bf4-3cf8ef9e05cc`. Any `/design-sync` push targets nothing. `componentSrcMap` enumerates 15 components and will need the 7 new primitives — but D-12 **defers** this. | **Deferred (D-12).** Note in the plan so a later executor does not "fix" it out of scope |

**The canonical question, answered:** the only runtime state carrying the old system is **build output and the cloud design project**. There is no database migration, no data backfill, and no re-registration. That is unusually clean for a migration phase and the plan should say so, so nobody budgets for a migration wave that has nothing to migrate.

## Validation Architecture

### Test Framework

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Framework | Vitest **4.1.10** (`@vitejs/plugin-react` 6.0.4, `jsdom` 30.0.1) |
| Config file | `vitest.config.ts` — `fileParallelism: false`, `sequence.concurrent: false` (deliberate: all files share one Postgres; **do not change**) |
| Quick run command | `pnpm exec vitest run <path>` |
| Full suite command | `pnpm exec vitest run` — **47 files / 462 tests / 50.06s, all green (2026-08-04)** |
| Build gate | `pnpm build` |
| Typecheck | `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` — **never `pnpm dlx tsc`** |
| ⚠ Vitest 4 gotcha | **`--reporter=basic` was removed** and errors with `Failed to load url basic`. Verified this session. Use the default reporter |

### Phase Requirements → Test Map

| SC | Behaviour | Test Type | Automated Command | File Exists? |
|----|-----------|-----------|-------------------|-------------|
| **SC1** | No third-party font/asset request on any page, one allowlisted exception | unit (source scan) | `pnpm exec vitest run tests/theme/no-third-party-assets.test.ts` | ❌ Wave 1 |
| **SC1** | Compiled CSS emits zero external `url()`/`@import` | integration (build output) | `pnpm build && pnpm exec vitest run tests/theme/build-assets.test.ts` | ❌ Wave 1 |
| **SC1** | RO/HU diacritics render in all three families | **manual-only** | visual check at 1× on a phone | n/a — glyph *coverage* is provable statically (see below); *rendering* is not |
| **SC2** | Phase 01 suite passes unchanged | regression | `pnpm exec vitest run` — must stay **462 green**, growing only by the 2 new D-13 tests | ✅ exists |
| **SC2** | Token layer does not shadow Tailwind's container scale | unit | `pnpm exec vitest run tests/lib/theme-width-scale.test.ts` | ✅ exists — **this is the token layer's tripwire** |
| **SC3** | Every Phase 01 surface renders in the new system | **manual-only** | `/gsd-ui-review` or a browser pass | n/a |
| **SC3** | Interactive controls meet the 44px touch floor | unit (token) + manual | assert `--spacing-touch: 44px` survives; assert the chosen phone control size ≥ 44px | partial — extend `theme-width-scale.test.ts`'s sibling, or a new `tests/theme/touch-targets.test.ts` |
| **SC4** | No venue theme value produces a sub-AA text/background pair | unit (exhaustive sweep) | `pnpm exec vitest run tests/theme/venue-contrast-guardrail.test.ts` | ❌ Wave 1 |
| **SC4** | Cena tokens never leak into the venue namespace | unit (source scan) | assert no `--szeged\|--napfeny\|--paprika\|--tisza` in `app/tokens/venue.css` | ❌ Wave 1 |
| **SC5** | Diner vocabulary exists and covers the named patterns | **structural (source scan) + manual** | assert the vocabulary artifacts exist and cover the 11 verdicts' residue | ❌ — see below |
| **SC5** | Allergen vocabulary is the full EU Annex II set | unit | `expect(ALLERGENS).toHaveLength(14)` + assert `peanuts` and `nuts` are distinct keys | ❌ Phase 3 — **but the vocabulary should be authored in 01.1 as part of the diner design vocabulary** |
| **D-13** | An EUR venue can be created | unit (jsdom + FormData) | `pnpm exec vitest run tests/venues/venue-eur-submission.test.tsx` | ❌ Wave 5 |

### What is measurable, at what layer, with what tool

| Claim | Measurable? | Layer | Tool | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| No third-party **font** request | **yes, fully** | source + build output | vitest reading `.next/static/chunks/*.css` | Already provably true: zero `https?://` matches today |
| No third-party **asset** request | **yes, with one allowlisted exception** | source scan of `app/`+`components/` | vitest + AST or regex over `<Script src>` / `<link href>` / `@import url()` | The exception is `https://accounts.google.com/gsi/client` (ACCT-01) |
| RO/HU **glyph coverage** | **yes** | build output | assert the emitted `@font-face` `unicode-range` blocks include 0x102-0x21B, or assert the `subsets` argument in `app/layout.tsx` includes `latin-ext` | The second is cheaper and adequate |
| RO/HU **rendering** | no | — | human | A subset can be correct and still look wrong |
| Contrast ≥ 4.5:1 for every reachable pair | **yes, exhaustively** | pure function | vitest sweep over the finite curated set | Complete only because D-03 made the pairing set finite |
| 462-test regression invariant | **yes** | full suite | `pnpm exec vitest run` | Two known-flaky files — re-run before believing a red |
| Every surface "renders in the new system" | no | — | human / `/gsd-ui-review` | No snapshot tests exist and adding them would couple the suite to appearance, which SC2 argues against |
| One-handed phone usability | partially | token + manual | 44px floor assertion + human | The floor is necessary, not sufficient |

### Sampling Rate

- **Per task commit:** `pnpm exec vitest run` on the touched area + `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit`
- **Per wave merge:** `pnpm exec vitest run` (full, ~50s) + `pnpm build`
- **Phase gate:** full suite green (462 + 2 new = **464**), `pnpm build` clean, SC1 + SC4 tripwires green, `/gsd-verify-work`

### Wave 0 Gaps

- [ ] `tests/theme/no-third-party-assets.test.ts` — SC1, allowlist of exactly one origin
- [ ] `tests/theme/build-assets.test.ts` — SC1 layer 2, reads `.next/static/chunks/*.css`
- [ ] `tests/theme/venue-contrast-guardrail.test.ts` — SC4 proof
- [ ] `tests/theme/token-boundary.test.ts` — SC4/D-02 (no Cena hue in the venue namespace) + D-10 (no dark selector on `--venue-*`)
- [ ] `tests/venues/venue-eur-submission.test.tsx` — G-01-13
- [ ] `tests/actions/create-venue-revalidation.test.ts` — G-01-14
- [ ] `lib/theme/contrast.ts`, `lib/theme/venue-tokens.ts` — the units under test
- [ ] `tests/format/money.test.ts` — pins `narrowSymbol` → `"lei"` and the 4-digit HUF grouping behaviour with literal expected strings (ICU data shifts between Node majors)
- [ ] `lib/format/money.ts` — `Intl.NumberFormat` wrapper (Pattern 10)
- [ ] No framework install needed; no shared-fixture file needed (the suite has no `conftest`-equivalent and tests are self-contained)

**SC5 is the weakest-measured criterion, and that should be stated in the plan rather than papered over.** "The diner menu has a mobile-first design vocabulary" is not a property a unit test can assert. What *is* assertable, and what the plan should use as the SC5 gate:

1. **The residue is enumerated, not assumed.** The 11 verdicts above name exactly what does not transfer. A structural check can assert that each named gap has either an artifact in the vocabulary or an explicit deferral row.
2. **The allergen vocabulary is 14** — a real unit test, and the one SC5-adjacent assertion with legal weight.
3. **The three D-07 / detected-language / allergen-disclaimer strings exist as Copywriting Contract rows** in all three languages — greppable against `01-UI-SPEC.md`, following the repo's existing source-scan test idiom.
4. Everything else — "mobile-first", "intentional and attractive" — is a human gate (`/gsd-ui-review`).

## Security Domain

`security_enforcement: true`, `security_asvs_level: 1`.

### Applicable ASVS Categories

| ASVS Category | Applies | Standard Control |
|---------------|---------|-----------------|
| V2 Authentication | **no** (not modified) | 01.1 re-skins `app/(auth)/*` but changes no auth logic. **Re-skinning must not alter the consent gate ordering (D-21) or the shared signup/login error message** — `COPY.errors.auth` is deliberately ambiguous to prevent account enumeration (T-02-01) |
| V3 Session Management | **no** | `IdleRelock` (D-07) is re-skinned; its timer must not move |
| V4 Access Control | **no** | `(dashboard)/layout.tsx` carries a documented staff/device gate (WR-03). **A re-skin must not touch that block** |
| **V5 Input Validation** | **YES** | `zod` 4.x. Two live surfaces: (a) the G-01-13 hidden input adds a *client-controllable* `enabledLanguages` value — already covered by `z.enum(SUPPORTED_LANGUAGE_CODES)`, an exact-ASCII enum chosen precisely so no Unicode normalisation can smuggle a lookalike; (b) the future venue-theme input, which must be validated to a strict grammar before reaching CSS |
| V6 Cryptography | **no** | none in scope |
| **V7 Error Handling / Logging** | **partial** | `COPY.errors.*` strings are security-relevant (enumeration resistance). The D-04 lexicon re-cut must not soften them |
| **V14 Configuration** | **YES** | SC1's third-party-request rule *is* a supply-chain and privacy control: a font CDN request is a personal-data transfer in a product built to need no consent banner |

### Known Threat Patterns for this stack

| Pattern | STRIDE | Standard Mitigation |
|---------|--------|---------------------|
| **CSS injection via a venue theme value** | Tampering | Constrain to `#rrggbb` at the Zod boundary; inject via React's `style` prop (escaped), **never** `<style dangerouslySetInnerHTML>`. This is the single new attack surface 01.1 creates |
| **Accessibility bypass on a legal gate** | Repudiation | THEME-04 must be enforced on the **write path** (Server Action + Zod), not client-only — a direct PostgREST/RPC caller bypasses the UI. Mirrors the existing `createVenueSchema` ↔ CHECK-constraint doctrine |
| Hidden-input value tampering (G-01-13 fix) | Tampering | Value is already re-validated server-side by `z.enum` + the `venues_enabled_languages_supported` CHECK. **No new exposure** — the hidden input carries a value the enabled checkbox would have carried anyway |
| Third-party script/font on a no-consent-banner product | Information Disclosure | SC1 tripwire with an explicit one-entry allowlist |
| Registry supply chain (`shadcn add`) | Tampering | Source is copied into the repo and reviewed in the diff — not a runtime dependency. Review the 7 added files as code, not as a lockfile bump |
| Over-broad `revalidatePath('/', 'layout')` | DoS (self-inflicted) | Purges the *client* Router Cache only; the dashboard layout is already dynamic. Negligible. If the diner ISR surface later shares a root, revisit |

## State of the Art

| Old Approach | Current Approach | When Changed | Impact on this phase |
|--------------|------------------|--------------|--------|
| `tailwind.config.js` + `@tailwind base/components/utilities` | `@import "tailwindcss"` + `@theme` in CSS | Tailwind v4 | The DS's `cena-theme.css` is already v4 — no translation needed |
| `@theme` for all tokens | **`@theme inline` when a token references another variable** | Tailwind v4 | **Required** for the venue theme to be nestable-overridable |
| `<link href="fonts.googleapis.com">` | `next/font/google` (build-time download, self-hosted) | Next 13 | Kills W-2 with zero custom tooling |
| shadcn `--style new-york` | `style` read from `components.json`; `new-york` removed; this repo is `radix-nova` | shadcn v3→v4 | `--style` on the CLI is gone |
| shadcn `form` + react-hook-form | `useActionState` + Zod + Server Actions | React 19 / Next 15+ | `shadcn add form` adds nothing here |
| `middleware.ts` | **`proxy.ts`** exporting `async function proxy` | Next 16 | Nothing in this phase touches it |
| `revalidatePath`/`revalidateTag` only | `updateTag` / `refresh` added for Cache Components | Next 16 | **Do not adopt** — CLAUDE.md prescribes `revalidatePath`, and no `cacheTag` exists on the venue read |
| Vitest `--reporter=basic` | removed | Vitest 4 | Verified error this session |
| WCAG 2.x contrast ratio | APCA in the WCAG 3 *draft* | ongoing | **Stay on WCAG 2.1** — SC4 names 4.5:1, which only WCAG 2.x defines |

**Deprecated / outdated in the inputs to this phase:**
- `DESIGN-SYSTEM.md`'s audit body (2026-08-02): the terracotta brand, the "diner surface does not exist" blocker, the 20-card guideline count, the 387/442-test figures. The dated delta at the top supersedes it; **the correct current figure is 47 files / 462 tests**.
- `01-UI-SPEC.md` frontmatter: `shadcn_initialized: false`, `preset: style=new-york` — both false now (`components.json` exists, style is `radix-nova`). If 01.1 edits this artifact for D-04, correcting the frontmatter is a cheap, in-scope truth repair.
- `.design-sync/config.json` `projectId` — points at a deleted project. **Deferred by D-12; do not fix in this phase.**

| # | Claim | Section | Risk if Wrong |

| A1 | Tailwind v4's PostCSS plugin processes `@theme` blocks inside files reached by `@import` from `globals.css` | Pattern 4 | Token layer must collapse into one file. Cheap to detect on first build; low risk |
| A2 | The DS's spacing scale reuses t-shirt names (`xs`…`3xl`) that collide with Tailwind's container scale | Pattern 4 / Pitfall 1 | If it uses numeric names, `theme-width-scale.test.ts` never fires and the shield section is dead weight. **Resolve with one `DesignSync(get_file)` on `tokens/spacing.css` at the start of Wave 1** — not blocking, but cheap and worth doing before the token layer is written |
| A3 | The DS's colour tokens are hex (not oklch) | Pattern 3 | If oklch, `culori` becomes necessary for the SC4 sweep. **Resolve with one `DesignSync(get_file)` on `tokens/colors.css` + `tokens/semantic.css` at the start of Wave 1.** Same fetch answers A14 |
| A4 | `Tag` in the DS is a static chip with no Radix behaviour | Pattern 7 | If it is interactive (removable/toggle), it is a `ToggleGroup` re-skin, not a hand-authored span |
| A5 | `Icon` in the DS is a stroke-width wrapper, not a sprite system | Pattern 7 | A sprite system would be materially more work |
| A6 | The venue colour control (THEME-02) yields a small number of inputs, not a free-form multi-token editor | Pattern 3 | A free-form editor makes the exhaustive sweep impossible; the guardrail would fall back to Zod-refinement + property testing. **This is the assumption most worth confirming with the user** |
| ~~A7~~ | ~~`templates/qr-menu/` genuinely covers *some* of its 11 claimed requirements~~ | — | **RESOLVED 2026-08-04.** Verified from the mirrored source: 1 holds, 10 partial, 0 does-not-hold. See `## Requirement Coverage Verdicts` |
| ~~A8~~ | ~~`DesignSync` is read-only~~ | — | **RESOLVED 2026-08-04.** `DesignSync` **can write** (`finalize_plan` → `write_files`). D-11 is a task, not a checkpoint — but it needs its own `finalize_plan` approval. See Pattern 11 |
| ~~A9~~ | ~~The D-12 archive list is still accurate~~ | — | **RESOLVED 2026-08-04.** Confirmed against the live manifest; all ten paths exist |
| A10 | Adding a hidden input alongside a disabled Radix checkbox does not disturb Radix's internal bubble-input sync | Pattern 5 | Low — the hidden input is an independent DOM node with no Radix awareness. Covered by the new test |
| A11 | OFL 1.1 permits self-hosting Google's own pre-built subsets without attribution in the UI | Pattern 1 | Standard practice; OFL requires the notice to travel with the *font software*, not the rendered page. If the team wants belt-and-braces, ship `OFL.txt` alongside — but `next/font` does not expose the files as a redistributable bundle, so this is low risk |
| **A12** | The DS's `Button variant="primary"` fill resolves from a **szeged ramp token**, not from `--accent` | Pattern 2 | If it does, the template's language pills put **Cena azure on the diner surface** and breach D-02 directly. Resolvable by fetching `components/Button` via `DesignSync` — cheap, and worth doing before Wave 3 |
| **A13** | `Badge tone="warning"` maps to **napfeny** | Pattern 2 | The README says the "Now" badge is "the one gold element per screen, per the napfeny rule", which strongly implies it. If so, Cena gold renders on every venue's menu — an open D-02 decision, not a defect. See Open Question 7 |
| **A14** | Every diner-surface colour in `tokens/semantic.css` is expressible as sRGB hex | Pattern 3 | Same risk as A3. If the semantic layer is oklch, the SC4 sweep needs `culori`. The template gives token *names* but not *values* |
| **A15** | The template's three-language `T` tables are of shippable translation quality | Cross-cutting | They read as idiomatic and were authored alongside HU-first menu content, but no native speaker has reviewed them in this session. Treat as a strong starting point requiring review, not as final copy |

## Open Questions (RESOLVED)

**All nine are closed as of 2026-08-05.** Q1 and Q2 were answered inside this research pass. Q3–Q9 were
answered in `01.1-UI-SPEC.md` (see its resolved-questions table, rows OQ3–OQ9) and each is now carried by a
named plan in `.planning/phases/01.1-design-system-migration/`. Nothing below is still awaiting a decision;
the `Recommendation:` lines are preserved as the reasoning that produced each answer, with the answer and its
owning plan marked inline.

1. ~~**Does the qr-menu template actually cover the 11 requirements it names?**~~ — **ANSWERED.** 1 holds, 10 partial, 0 does-not-hold. See `## Requirement Coverage Verdicts`.

2. ~~**Can `DesignSync` write, or is D-11 a manual step?**~~ — **ANSWERED.** It can write (`finalize_plan` → `write_files`). D-11 is a task with its own approval gate. See Pattern 11.

7. **Does the allergen gap change Phase 3's scope, or 01.1's?** — **RESOLVED: 01.1 owns the vocabulary, Phase 3 owns the filtering.** The 14-key Annex II vocabulary in three languages is authored in **plan 01.1-04, task 1** (`lib/allergens.ts`); DINE-06 filtering stays in Phase 3. Cena models Annex II's 14 **categories**, which is what the regulation mandates and what a restaurant can realistically maintain. See `01.1-UI-SPEC.md` row OQ7.
   - What we know: the template ships 7 of Annex II's 14; the README's "Allergens are the EU set" claim is false; PROJECT.md makes allergen correctness a named legal constraint and a release gate.
   - What's unclear: whether the 14-value vocabulary is part of 01.1's "diner design vocabulary" (SC5 names "allergen and dietary display") or Phase 3's DINE-06 implementation.
   - Recommendation: **author the vocabulary in 01.1**, implement the filtering in Phase 3. The vocabulary is a token/copy artifact — 14 keys × 3 languages — which is exactly what SC5 asks for, it is cheap, and leaving it to Phase 3 repeats the pattern D-06 was written to prevent (a legal gate invented under time pressure). Note it also needs a decision on whether Cena models Annex II's 14 *categories* or a finer ingredient list; the categories are what the regulation mandates and what a restaurant can realistically maintain.

8. **Are status colours (warning / danger / success) Cena-fixed or venue-themable on the diner surface?** — **RESOLVED: Cena-fixed, permanently, on every surface — and permanently in the SC4 contrast sweep.** Carried by **plans 01.1-06, 01.1-07 and 01.1-08**: 06 fixes the status families outside the venue-themable namespace, 07 and 08 consume them. Pairs 11 and 17 stay in the sweep against venue-controlled paper. See `01.1-UI-SPEC.md` row OQ8.
   - What we know: the "Now" badge is `Badge tone="warning"` — described by the README as "the one gold element per screen, per the napfeny rule" — and the DINE-04 banner uses the `--warning-*` family. So Cena's napfeny gold currently renders on a venue-branded menu.
   - What's unclear: D-02 forbids *azure* on the diner surface and says colour varies per venue. It does not say which side status colours fall on.
   - Recommendation: **Cena-fixed, and say so in the contract.** A warning that reads as a warning is a safety affordance — sold-out, allergen, stale menu — and a venue that themes it can accidentally make it invisible. But every status pair must then sit in the SC4 contrast set against venue-controlled paper (pairs 11 and 17 in Pattern 3). Surface to the user, because it is a visible brand decision, not a purely technical one.

9. **Does the QR payload encode the language?** — **RESOLVED: yes — `/menu/[slug]/[defaultLang]`, against a `/menu/[slug]/[lang]` static page set, with `/menu/[slug]` negotiating `Accept-Language` as a 307 in `proxy.ts`.** Decided in `01.1-UI-SPEC.md` § Language (LANG-05, LANG-06) and row OQ9. 01.1 builds no route, so the decision is *recorded* rather than implemented: **plan 01.1-04, task 2** writes it into `lib/diner-copy.ts`'s header — the module that owns the `languageDetected` string which only exists because negotiation is a 307 — and **plan 01.1-14, task 3** puts it on the phase record as a carried-forward decision, distinct from the phase's four honest gaps. Owners downstream: DINE-01 (Phase 2) generates the payload, LANG-05/06 (Phase 5) build the routing.
   - What we know: Pattern 9's redirect costs one RTT on the connection DINE-03 is about. Encoding the venue's default language in the QR removes it for the common case.
   - What's unclear: ~~whether DINE-01's QR generation (Phase 2) wants a language segment in the URL it encodes.~~ — settled; it does.
   - Recommendation: decide in 01.1's vocabulary work, because it constrains the URL shape that both LANG-05/06 and DINE-01 depend on. It is free if decided now and a migration if decided later. **Followed.** The migration cost is understated above: a QR code is printed, laminated and stuck to a table, so a change after DINE-01 ships is a physical re-print of every table in every venue, not a code change.

3. **Is the venue colour control a curated palette set or a free-hex picker?** (assumption A6) — **RESOLVED: neither is assumed — `resolveVenueTheme()` is built as a TOTAL function that derives text tokens rather than accepting them, so it works for both shapes.** Carried by **plan 01.1-06**. See `01.1-UI-SPEC.md` row OQ3.
   - What we know: THEME-02 says "colour palette"; PROJECT.md says "templates plus guardrailed brand controls" and excludes deep customisation.
   - What's unclear: which shape.
   - Recommendation: **design the guardrail for the harder case** — `resolveVenueTheme()` as a total function that derives text tokens rather than accepting them. That works for both shapes, and makes the exhaustive sweep a *bonus* under the curated shape rather than a dependency on it.

4. **Does SC1 mean "no third-party asset" literally, or "no third-party font/CSS asset"?** — **RESOLVED: an allowlist with exactly ONE entry (`accounts.google.com/gsi/client`) plus an inline ACCT-01 justification, with the tension surfaced rather than quietly narrowed.** Carried by **plan 01.1-05**. See `01.1-UI-SPEC.md` row OQ4.
   - What we know: `GoogleOneTap` loads `https://accounts.google.com/gsi/client`, and that is ACCT-01, a shipped feature.
   - Recommendation: **allowlist with exactly one entry and an inline ACCT-01 justification.** Surface the tension to the user in the plan rather than quietly narrowing the check — quietly narrowing it is how a green tripwire stops meaning anything.

5. **Does SC2's "all 16 primitives" intend to include `alert`, `avatar` and `dropdown-menu`?** — **RESOLVED: re-skin all 19, and note the discrepancy in the plan so a verifier reads neither scope creep nor under-delivery.** Carried by **plan 01.1-08**. See `01.1-UI-SPEC.md` row OQ5.
   - What we know: all three ship in Phase 01 surfaces; none is in the DS's 16.
   - Recommendation: re-skin all 19. Note the discrepancy in the plan so the verifier does not read 19 as scope creep or 16 as an under-delivery.

6. **What phone control height satisfies SC3?** — **RESOLVED: a 44px floor on every control on every surface, decided in the TOKEN wave rather than the surface wave.** Carried by **plan 01.1-05** (wave 2, with the tokens), not by the wave-4 surface plans — deciding it late would have made it a rework of every screen. See `01.1-UI-SPEC.md` row OQ6.
   - What we know: `radix-nova` Button ships 24–36px; the DS mandates 44px; `--spacing-touch: 44px` already exists and is pinned by an existing test.
   - Recommendation: decide in **Wave 1**, with the tokens — not in Wave 4 with the surfaces, when it becomes a rework of every screen.
